algorithm.description: The algorithm used by the underlying analytic to generate the finding.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the analytic that generated the finding.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the analytic that generated the finding.

@deprecated.message: Related Analytics has been decoupled from this object, instead use finding_info.related_analytics.

related_analytics.caption: Related Analytics
related_analytics.description: Other analytics related to this analytic.

sensor_info_list.caption: Sensor Information List
sensor_info_list.description: An array of sensor_info objects, each describing a sensor control point analyzed or correlated by the analytic. Each element typically represents a source of related_events that contributed to the finding. An individual sensor control point may also directly originate the finding, though more commonly it emits alerts that a downstream consumer treats as findings.

1.caption: Active
1.description: The Analytic is active.

2.caption: Suppressed
2.description: The Analytic is suppressed. For example, a user/customer has suppressed a particular detection signature in a security product.

3.caption: Experimental
3.description: The Analytic is still under development and considered experimental.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The state is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The analytic type.

1.caption: Rule
1.description: A Rule in security analytics refers to predefined criteria or conditions set to monitor, alert, or enforce policies, playing a crucial role in access control, threat detection, and regulatory compliance across security systems.

10.caption: Partial Data Match
10.description: Partial Data Match involves identifying instances where segments of sensitive information or patterns match, facilitating nuanced DLP and threat detection without requiring complete data conformity.

11.caption: Indexed Data Match
11.description: Indexed Data Match refers to comparing content against a pre-compiled index of sensitive information to efficiently detect and prevent unauthorized access or breaches, streamlining DLP and compliance efforts.

2.caption: Behavioral
2.description: Behavioral analytics focus on monitoring and analyzing user or system actions to identify deviations from established patterns, aiding in the detection of insider threats, fraud, and advanced persistent threats (APTs).

3.caption: Statistical
3.description: Statistical analytics pertains to analyzing data patterns and anomalies using statistical models to predict, detect, and respond to potential threats, enhancing overall security posture through informed decision-making.

4.caption: Learning (ML/DL)
4.description: Learning (ML/DL) encompasses techniques that can "learn" from known data to create analytics that generalize to new data. There may be a statistical component to these techniques, but it is not a requirement.

5.caption: Fingerprinting
5.description: Fingerprinting is the technique of collecting detailed system data, including software versions and configurations, to enhance threat detection, data loss prevention (DLP), and endpoint detection and response (EDR) capabilities.

6.caption: Tagging
6.description: Tagging refers to the practice of assigning labels or identifiers to data, users, assets, or activities to monitor, control access, and facilitate incident response across various security domains such as DLP and EDR.

7.caption: Keyword Match
7.description: Keyword Match involves scanning content for specific terms to identify sensitive information, potential threats, or policy violations, aiding in DLP and compliance monitoring.

8.caption: Regular Expressions
8.description: Regular Expressions are used to define complex search patterns for identifying, validating, and extracting specific data sets or threats within digital content, enhancing DLP, EDR, and threat detection mechanisms.

9.caption: Exact Data Match
9.description: Exact Data Match is a precise comparison technique used to detect the unauthorized use or exposure of specific, sensitive information, crucial for enforcing DLP policies and protecting against data breaches.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the analytic that generated the finding.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

analytic.caption: Analytic
analytic.description: The Analytic object contains details about the analytic technique used to analyze and derive insights from the data or information that led to the creation of a finding or conclusion.
analytic.name: analytic

observation_parameter.caption: Observation Parameter
observation_parameter.description: The specific parameter, metric or property where the anomaly was observed. Examples include: CPU usage percentage, API response time in milliseconds, HTTP error rate, memory utilization, network latency, transaction volume, etc. This helps identify the exact aspect of the system exhibiting anomalous behavior.

observation_type.caption: Observation Type
observation_type.description: The type of analysis methodology used to detect the anomaly. This indicates how the anomaly was identified through different analytical approaches. Common types include: Frequency Analysis, Time Pattern Analysis, Volume Analysis, Sequence Analysis, Distribution Analysis, etc.

observations.caption: Observations
observations.description: Details about the observed anomaly or observations that were flagged as anomalous compared to expected baseline behavior.

observed_pattern.caption: Observed Pattern
observed_pattern.description: The specific pattern identified within the observation type. For Frequency Analysis, this could be 'FREQUENT', 'INFREQUENT', 'RARE', or 'UNSEEN'. For Time Pattern Analysis, this could be 'BUSINESS_HOURS', 'OFF_HOURS', or 'UNUSUAL_TIME'. For Volume Analysis, this could be 'NORMAL_VOLUME', 'HIGH_VOLUME', or 'SURGE'. The pattern values are specific to each observation type and indicate how the observed behavior relates to the baseline.

anomaly.caption: Anomaly
anomaly.description: Describes an anomaly or deviation detected in a system. Anomalies are unexpected activity patterns that could indicate potential issues needing attention.
anomaly.name: anomaly

analysis_targets.caption: Analysis Targets
analysis_targets.description: The analysis targets define the scope of monitored activities, specifying what entities, systems or processes are analyzed for activity patterns.

anomalies.caption: Anomalies
anomalies.description: List of detected activities that significantly deviate from the established baselines. This can include unusual access patterns, unexpected user-agents, abnormal API usage, suspicious traffic spikes, unauthorized access attempts, and other activities that may indicate potential security threats or system issues.

baselines.caption: Baselines
baselines.description: List of established patterns representing normal activity that serve as reference points for anomaly detection. This includes typical user interaction patterns like common user-agents, expected API access frequencies and patterns, standard resource utilization levels, and regular traffic flows. These baselines help establish what constitutes 'normal' activity in the system.

anomaly_analysis.caption: Anomaly Analysis
anomaly_analysis.description: Describes the analysis of activity patterns and anomalies of target entities to identify potential security threats, performance issues, or other deviations from established baselines. This includes monitoring and analyzing user interactions, API usage, resource utilization, access patterns and other measured indicators.
anomaly_analysis.name: anomaly_analysis

group.caption: Group
group.description: The information pertaining to the API group.

request.caption: API Request Details
request.description: Details pertaining to the API request.

response.caption: API Response Details
response.description: Details pertaining to the API response.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The information pertaining to the API service.

token.caption: Token
token.description: The API or client token used to authenticate or authorize the API request. This attribute contains the base token object that represents: (1) IdP-issued client tokens (type_id: 6) such as Okta API tokens or Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, or (2) generic API tokens/keys (type_id: 7) used for SaaS application authentication. Use this attribute when the API request was authenticated using a token that should be tracked as part of the API activity event. Note: Protocol-specific authentication tokens (Kerberos, OIDC, SAML) should be represented using authentication_token in authentication events, not in API activity events.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the API service.

api.caption: API
api.description: The API, or Application Programming Interface, object represents  information pertaining to an API request and response.
api.name: api

criticality.caption: Business Criticality
criticality.description: The criticality of the application as defined by the event source.

desc.caption: Application Description
desc.description: A description or commentary for an application, usually retrieved from an upstream system.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The name of the related application or associated resource group.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the application.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the application.

name.caption: Application Name
name.description: The name of the application.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the application.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The software product that this application is an instance of, carrying product identity such as vendor_name, cpe_name, and canonical version.

resource_relationship.caption: Application Relationship
resource_relationship.description: A graph representation showing how this application relates to and interacts with other entities in the environment. This can include parent/child relationships, dependencies, or other connections.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

sbom.caption: Related SBOM
sbom.description: The Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) associated with the application

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the application.

type.caption: Application Type
type.description: The type of application as defined by the event source, e.g., GitHub, Azure Logic App, or Amazon Elastic BeanStalk.

uid.caption: Application ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the application.

uid_alt.caption: Application Alternative ID
uid_alt.description: An alternative or contextual identifier for the application, such as a configuration, organization, or license UID.

version.caption: Application Version
version.description: The semantic version of the application, e.g., 1.7.4.

application.caption: Application
application.description: An Application describes the details for an inventoried application as reported by an Application Security tool or other Developer-centric tooling. Applications can be defined as Kubernetes resources, Containerized resources, or application hosting-specific cloud sources such as AWS Elastic BeanStalk, AWS Lightsail, or Azure Logic Apps.
application.name: application

mitigation.caption: MITRE Mitigation
mitigation.description: The Mitigation object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Mitigation ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.

sub_technique.caption: MITRE Sub-technique
sub_technique.description: The Sub-technique object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Sub-technique ID and/or name associated to an attack.

tactic.caption: MITRE Tactic
tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the Tactic ID and/or name associated to an attack.

tactics.caption: Tactics
tactics.description: The Tactics associated with the attack technique.

technique.caption: MITRE Technique
technique.description: The Technique object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Technique ID and/or name associated to an attack.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Matrix version.

attack.caption: Attack Tactics & Techniques
attack.description: The Attack object describes the tactic, technique, sub-technique & mitigation associated to an attack.
attack.name: attack

device.caption: Device
device.description: Device used to complete an authentication request.

email_addr.caption: Email Address
email_addr.description: The email address used in an email-based authentication factor.

factor_type.caption: Factor Type
factor_type.description: The type of authentication factor used in an authentication attempt.

factor_type_id.caption: Factor Type ID
factor_type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the authentication factor.

1.caption: SMS
1.description: User receives and inputs a code sent to their mobile device via SMS text message.

10.caption: WebAuthn
10.description: Web-based API that enables users to register devices as authentication factors.

11.caption: Password
11.description: The user enters a password that they have previously established.

2.caption: Security Question
2.description: The user responds to a security question as part of a question-based authentication factor

3.caption: Phone Call
3.description: System calls the user's registered phone number and requires the user to answer and provide a response.

4.caption: Biometric
4.description: Devices that verify identity-based on user's physical identifiers, such as fingerprint scanners or retina scanners.

5.caption: Push Notification
5.description: Push notification is sent to user's registered device and requires the user to acknowledge.

6.caption: Hardware Token
6.description: Physical device that generates a code to be used for authentication.

7.caption: OTP
7.description: Application generates a one-time password (OTP) for use in authentication.

8.caption: Email
8.description: A code or link is sent to a user's registered email address.

9.caption: U2F
9.description: Typically involves a hardware token, which the user physically interacts with to authenticate.

is_hotp.caption: HMAC-based One-time Password (HOTP)
is_hotp.description: Whether the authentication factor is an HMAC-based One-time Password (HOTP).

is_totp.caption: Time-based One-time Password (TOTP)
is_totp.description: Whether the authentication factor is a Time-based One-time Password (TOTP).

phone_number.caption: Phone Number
phone_number.description: The phone number used for a telephony-based authentication request.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The name of provider for an authentication factor.

security_questions.caption: Security Questions
security_questions.description: The question(s) provided to user for a question-based authentication factor.

auth_factor.caption: Authentication Factor
auth_factor.description: An Authentication Factor object describes a category of methods used for identity verification in an authentication attempt.
auth_factor.name: auth_factor

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the Identity/Access management policies that are applicable.

authorization.caption: Authorization Result
authorization.description: The Authorization Result object provides details about the authorization outcome and associated policies related to activity.
authorization.name: authorization

name.caption: Name
name.description: Organization name for the Autonomous System.

number.caption: Number
number.description: Unique number that the AS is identified by.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: An autonomous system (AS) is a collection of connected Internet Protocol (IP) routing prefixes under the control of one or more network operators on behalf of a single administrative entity or domain that presents a common, clearly defined routing policy to the internet.
autonomous_system.name: autonomous_system

observation_parameter.caption: Observation Parameter
observation_parameter.description: The specific parameter or property being monitored. Examples include: CPU usage percentage, API response time in milliseconds, HTTP error rate, memory utilization, network latency, transaction volume, etc.

observation_type.caption: Observation Type
observation_type.description: The type of analysis being performed to establish baseline behavior. Common types include: Frequency Analysis, Time Pattern Analysis, Volume Analysis, Sequence Analysis, Distribution Analysis, etc.

observations.caption: Observations
observations.description: Collection of actual measured values, data points and observations recorded for this baseline.

observed_pattern.caption: Observed Pattern
observed_pattern.description: The specific pattern identified within the observation type. For Frequency Analysis, this could be 'FREQUENT', 'INFREQUENT', 'RARE', or 'UNSEEN'. For Time Pattern Analysis, this could be 'BUSINESS_HOURS', 'OFF_HOURS', or 'UNUSUAL_TIME'. For Volume Analysis, this could be 'NORMAL_VOLUME', 'HIGH_VOLUME', or 'SURGE'. The pattern values are specific to each observation type and indicate the baseline behavior.

baseline.caption: Baseline
baseline.description: Describes the baseline or expected behavior of a system, service, or component based on historical observations and measurements. It establishes reference points for comparison to detect anomalies, trends, and deviations from typical patterns.
baseline.name: baseline

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the certificate was created.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the certificate.

fingerprints.caption: Fingerprints
fingerprints.description: The fingerprint list of the certificate.

is_self_signed.caption: Certificate Self-Signed
is_self_signed.description: Denotes whether a digital certificate is self-signed or signed by a known certificate authority (CA).

sans.caption: Subject Alternative Names
sans.description: The list of subject alternative names that are secured by a specific certificate.

serial_number.caption: Certificate Serial Number
serial_number.description: The serial number of the certificate used to create the digital signature.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the certificate.

certificate.caption: Digital Certificate
certificate.description: The Digital Certificate, also known as a Public Key Certificate, object contains information about the ownership and usage of a public key. It serves as a means to establish trust in the authenticity and integrity of the public key and the associated entity.
certificate.name: certificate

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The CIS Control description. For example: Uninstall or disable unnecessary services on enterprise assets and software, such as an unused file sharing service, web application module, or service function.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The CIS Control name. For example: 4.8 Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CIS Control version. For example: v8.

cis_control.caption: CIS Control
cis_control.description: The CIS Control (aka Critical Security Control) object describes a prioritized set of actions to protect your organization and data from cyber-attack vectors. The CIS Controls are defined by the Center for Internet Security.
cis_control.name: cis_control

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Commit hash of image created for docker or the SHA256 hash of the container. For example: 13550340a8681c84c861aac2e5b440161c2b33a3e4f302ac680ca5b686de48de.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The container image used as a template to run the container.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the container.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The container name.

network_driver.caption: Network Driver
network_driver.description: The network driver used by the container. For example, bridge, overlay, host, none, etc.

orchestrator.caption: Orchestrator
orchestrator.description: The orchestrator managing the container, such as ECS, EKS, K8s, or OpenShift.

pod_uuid.caption: Pod UUID
pod_uuid.description: The unique identifier of the pod (or equivalent) that the container is executing on.

runtime.caption: Runtime
runtime.description: The backend running the container, such as containerd or cri-o.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of the container image.

tag.caption: Image Tag
tag.description: The tag used by the container. It can indicate version, format, OS.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the container.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The full container unique identifier for this instantiation of the container. For example: ac2ea168264a08f9aaca0dfc82ff3551418dfd22d02b713142a6843caa2f61bf.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The Container object describes an instance of a specific container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.
container.name: container

cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The number of processing cores or compute units for the component.

cpu_architecture.caption: CPU Architecture
cpu_architecture.description: The CPU architecture, normalized to the caption of the cpu_architecture_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

cpu_architecture_id.caption: CPU Architecture ID
cpu_architecture_id.description: The normalized identifier of the CPU architecture.

1.caption: x86
1.description: CPU uses the x86 ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

2.caption: ARM
2.description: CPU uses the ARM ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

3.caption: RISC-V
3.description: CPU uses the RISC-V ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The CPU architecture is not mapped. See the cpu_architecture attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The number of bits used by the CPU for memory addressing.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the CPU. For example: Intel Xeon Gold 6348, AMD EPYC 7763, or Apple M3 Max.

speed_mhz.caption: Compute Unit Speed (MHz)
speed_mhz.description: The nominal clock speed of the unit, expressed in megahertz.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the CPU. For example: Intel, AMD, or Apple.

cpu_info.caption: CPU Information
cpu_info.description: The CPU information object contains attributes describing a physical CPU package installed in the device.
cpu_info.name: cpu_info

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

cvss.caption: CVSS Score
cvss.description: The CVSS object details Common Vulnerability Scoring System scores from the advisory that are related to the vulnerability.

cwe.caption: CWE
cwe.description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.

cwe_uid.caption: CWE UID
cwe_uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) unique identifier. For example: CWE-787.

cwe_url.caption: CWE URL
cwe_url.description: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) definition URL. For example: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A brief description of the CVE Record.

epss.caption: EPSS
epss.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) object describes the estimated probability a vulnerability will be exploited. EPSS is a community-driven effort to combine descriptive information about vulnerabilities (CVEs) with evidence of actual exploitation in-the-wild.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the CVE Record.

related_cwes.caption: Related CWEs
related_cwes.description: Describes the Common Weakness Enumeration details related to the CVE Record.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the CVE record.

type.caption: Vulnerability Type
type.description:
The vulnerability type as classified in the CVE catalog.

Most frequently used vulnerability types are: DoS, Code Execution, Overflow, Memory Corruption, Sql Injection, XSS, Directory Traversal, Http Response Splitting, Bypass something, Gain Information, Gain Privileges, CSRF, File Inclusion. For more information see Vulnerabilities By Type distributions.

uid.caption: CVE ID
uid.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures unique number assigned to a specific computer vulnerability. A CVE Identifier begins with 4 digits representing the year followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CVE-2021-12345.

cve.caption: CVE
cve.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) object represents publicly disclosed cybersecurity vulnerabilities defined in CVE Program catalog (CVE). There is one CVE Record for each vulnerability in the catalog.
cve.name: cve

base_score.caption: Base Score
base_score.description: The CVSS base score. For example: 9.1.

depth.caption: CVSS Depth
depth.description: The CVSS depth represents a depth of the equation used to calculate CVSS score.

metrics.caption: Metrics
metrics.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System metrics. This attribute contains information on the CVE's impact. If the CVE has been analyzed, this attribute will contain any CVSSv2 or CVSSv3 information associated with the vulnerability. For example: { {"Access Vector", "Network"}, {"Access Complexity", "Low"}, ...}.

overall_score.caption: Overall Score
overall_score.description: The CVSS overall score, impacted by base, temporal, and environmental metrics. For example: 9.1.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description:
The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Qualitative Severity Rating. A textual representation of the numeric score.

CVSS v2.0
  • Low (0.0 – 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 – 6.9)
  • High (7.0 – 10.0)

CVSS v3.0
  • None (0.0)
  • Low (0.1 - 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 - 6.9)
  • High (7.0 - 8.9)
  • Critical (9.0 - 10.0)

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL for the CVSS score. For example: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228

vector_string.caption: Vector String
vector_string.description: The CVSS vector string is a text representation of a set of CVSS metrics. It is commonly used to record or transfer CVSS metric information in a concise form. For example: 3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor that provided the CVSS score. For example: NVD, REDHAT etc.

cvss.caption: CVSS Score
cvss.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) object provides a way to capture the principal characteristics of a vulnerability and produce a numerical score reflecting its severity.

issuer_uid.caption: Issuer ID
issuer_uid.description: The unique identifier of the trusted issuing authority (e.g., an OAuth authorization server, cloud STS, IAM broker, orchestration gateway, or SDK wrapper) that generated this delegation. Enables verification that delegation IDs were issued by an authorized component rather than self-asserted by the delegate.

parent_uid.caption: Parent Delegation ID
parent_uid.description: The delegation identifier of the parent delegation, if this delegation was created by re-delegating authority to another party (e.g., a downstream service or automated process). This creates a parent-child relationship that enables tracking the complete chain of delegation ancestry. Does not indicate that the delegate was instantiated or spawned by the parent's delegate; that relationship, if any, is tracked separately.

uid.caption: Delegation ID
uid.description: Unique identifier for this delegation context. Must be stable across the lifetime of the delegation and generated by a trusted issuing authority (e.g., an OAuth authorization server, cloud STS, IAM broker, or orchestration gateway) rather than self-asserted by the delegate. All events executed under this delegation share this identifier.

delegation.caption: Delegation
delegation.description: A durable authorization context that a principal issues to a delegate (e.g., an application, automated process, service account, or AI agent), representing delegated authority to act on the principal's behalf. Persists independently of any single trace, session, or workflow instance, so the same delegation can be referenced across many events. The principal and delegate themselves are identified by the other objects on the event carrying this delegation, such as actor.user or actor.iam_role for the principal and ai_operation.ai_agent for an AI delegate. The delegation object itself only carries the durable identifiers used to correlate across those events. Delegations reference a parent via parent_uid, forming a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of re-delegations that supports lineage queries across the chain of authority. This authority graph is distinct from any agent instantiation or orchestration hierarchy, which may or may not coincide with it.
delegation.name: delegation

algorithm_id.caption: Algorithm ID
algorithm_id.description: The identifier of the normalized digital signature algorithm.

1.caption: DSA
1.description: Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA).

2.caption: RSA
2.description: Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA) Algorithm.

3.caption: ECDSA
3.description: Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm.

4.caption: Authenticode
4.description: Authenticode Digital Signature Algorithm.

references.description: Windows Authenticode Portable Executable Signature Format (Microsoft, 2008)

5.caption: Code Signing
5.description: Code Signing Algorithm.

6.caption: App Package
6.description: Application Package Signing Algorithm.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The algorithm is not mapped. See the algorithm attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

certificate.caption: Certificate
certificate.description: The certificate object containing information about the digital certificate.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the digital signature was created.

developer_uid.caption: Developer UID
developer_uid.description: The developer ID on the certificate that signed the file.

digest.caption: Message Digest
digest.description: The message digest attribute contains the fixed length message hash representation and the corresponding hashing algorithm information.

serialization.caption: Serialization
serialization.description: The canonical serialization or signing-envelope scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was signed, normalized to the caption of serialization_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

serialization_id.caption: Serialization ID
serialization_id.description: The identifier of the normalized canonical serialization or signing-envelope scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was signed. A verifier must apply the same scheme to reproduce the signing input. Use Flat where the signed data is an opaque byte sequence, such as file content, to which no canonical serialization was applied. Distinct from algorithm_id, which identifies how the resulting bytes were signed; some signing formats (e.g. Authenticode) define their own canonicalization and populate both fields.

1.caption: Flat
1.description: No canonical serialization or signing envelope was applied; the signature is computed over the data's raw byte sequence, such as the content of a disk file or any other opaque byte stream.

2.caption: JCS
2.description: JSON Canonicalization Scheme - deterministic JSON serialization of the structured data prior to signing.

3.caption: JWS
3.description: JSON Web Signature - the JWS Signing Input, i.e. BASE64URL(protected header) '.' BASE64URL(payload).

4.caption: COSE
4.description: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption - the CBOR Sig_structure used as the binary signing input.

5.caption: DSSE
5.description: Dead Simple Signing Envelope - the PAE (Pre-Authentication Encoding) canonical signing input. Note: DSSE is a signing-envelope scheme, not a hash algorithm; any payload hash is carried separately in the fingerprint object.

6.caption: Authenticode
6.description: The Portable Executable (PE) Image Hash procedure that canonicalizes the PE structure into the byte sequence fed to the digest, excluding specified header fields and digesting sections in a defined order. Authenticode bundles canonicalization and signing format: when used, algorithm_id is also set to the Authenticode enum value.

references.description: Windows Authenticode Portable Executable Signature Format (Microsoft, 2008)

7.caption: Code Signing
7.description: The procedure that describes how hashes of code and other structures form the Code Directory message that is signed. When used, algorithm_id is also set to the Code Signing enum value.

8.caption: App Package
8.description: The Windows Application Package signing procedure that describes how file hashes are stored in the manifest, and how that manifest is signed.

state.caption: State
state.description: The digital signature state defines the signature state, normalized to the caption of 'state_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

state_id.caption: State ID
state_id.description: The normalized identifier of the signature state.

1.caption: Valid
1.description: The digital signature is valid.

10.caption: Broken
10.description: The digital signature is malformed and could not be processed.

2.caption: Expired
2.description: The digital signature is invalid because its timestamp does not fall within the certificate's validity period.

3.caption: Revoked
3.description: The digital signature is invalid due to certificate revocation.

4.caption: Suspended
4.description: The digital signature is invalid due to certificate suspension.

5.caption: Pending
5.description: The digital signature state is pending.

6.caption: Untrusted
6.description: The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is rooted in an untrusted CA or is an untrusted self-signed certificate.

7.caption: Distrusted
7.description: The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is explicitly distrusted. Note that whereas revocation is global, distrust reflects local IT/security policy.

8.caption: WrongUsage
8.description: The digital signature is invalid because the certificate is not intended for code signing purposes.

9.caption: Bad
9.description: The digital signature is cryptographically invalid, e.g. a mismatched digest. This indicates possible tampering.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The state is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

edge.caption: Edge
edge.description: Represents a connection or relationship between two nodes in a graph.

bcc.caption: Bcc
bcc.description: The machine-readable email header Bcc values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

bcc_mailboxes.caption: Bcc Mailboxes
bcc_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Bcc Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

cc.caption: Cc
cc.description: The machine-readable email header Cc values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

cc_mailboxes.caption: Cc Mailboxes
cc_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Cc Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

delivered_to.caption: Delivered To
delivered_to.description: The machine-readable Delivered-To email header field. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

delivered_to_list.caption: Delivered To List
delivered_to_list.description: The machine-readable Delivered-To email header values. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

files.caption: Files
files.description: The files embedded or attached to the email.

from.caption: From
from.description: The machine-readable email header From value, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

from_list.caption: From List
from_list.description: The machine-readable email header From values. This array should contain the value in from. For example example.user@usersdomain.com.

from_mailbox.caption: From Mailbox
from_mailbox.description: The human-readable email header From Mailbox value. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

from_mailboxes.caption: From Mailboxes
from_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header From Mailbox values. This array should contain the value in from_mailbox. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

http_headers.caption: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

is_read.caption: Read
is_read.description: The indication of whether the email has been read.

message_uid.caption: Message UID
message_uid.description: The email header Message-ID value, as defined by RFC 5322.

reply_to.caption: Reply To
reply_to.description: The machine-readable email header Reply-To value, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

reply_to_list.caption: Reply To List
reply_to_list.description: The machine-readable email header Reply-To values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

reply_to_mailboxes.caption: Reply To Mailboxes
reply_to_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Reply To Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

return_path.caption: Return Path
return_path.description: The address found in the 'Return-Path' header, which indicates where bounce messages (non-delivery reports) should be sent. This address is often set by the sending system and may differ from the 'From' or 'Sender' addresses. For example, mailer-daemon@senderserver.com.

sender.caption: Sender
sender.description: The machine readable email address of the system or server that actually transmitted the email message, extracted from the email headers per RFC 5322. This differs from the from field, which shows the message author. The sender field is most commonly used when multiple addresses appear in the from_list field, or when the transmitting system is different from the message author (such as when sending on behalf of someone else).

sender_mailbox.caption: Sender Mailbox
sender_mailbox.description: The human readable email address of the system or server that actually transmitted the email message, extracted from the email headers per RFC 5322. This differs from the from_mailbox field, which shows the message author. The sender mailbox field is most commonly used when multiple addresses appear in the from_mailboxes field, or when the transmitting system is different from the message author (such as when sending on behalf of someone else).

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes of the email, including attachments.

smtp_from.caption: SMTP From
smtp_from.description: The value of the SMTP MAIL FROM command.

smtp_to.caption: SMTP To
smtp_to.description: The value of the SMTP envelope RCPT TO command.

subject.caption: Subject
subject.description: The email header Subject value, as defined by RFC 5322.

to.caption: To
to.description: The machine-readable email header To values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

to_mailboxes.caption: To Mailboxes
to_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header To Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

uid.caption: Email Thread UID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the email thread.

urls.caption: URLs
urls.description: The URLs embedded in the email.

x_originating_ip.caption: X-Originating-IP
x_originating_ip.description: The X-Originating-IP header identifying the emails originating IP address(es).

email.caption: Email
email.description: The Email object describes the email metadata such as sender, recipients, and direction, and can include embedded URLs and files.
email.name: email

algorithm.caption: Encryption Algorithm
algorithm.description: The encryption algorithm used, normalized to the caption of 'algorithm_id

1.caption: DES

2.caption: TripleDES

3.caption: AES

6.description: ShangMi Cryptographic Algorithm

key_length.caption: Encryption Key Length
key_length.description: The length of the encryption key used.

key_uid.caption: Key UID
key_uid.description: The unique identifier of the key used for encryption. For example, AWS KMS Key ARN.

type.caption: Encryption Type
type.description: The type of the encryption used.

encryption_details.caption: Encryption Details
encryption_details.description: Details about the encryption methodology utilized.
encryption_details.name: encryption_details

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the enrichment data was generated.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The enrichment data associated with the attribute and value. The meaning of this data depends on the type the enrichment record.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A long description of the enrichment data.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the attribute to which the enriched data pertains.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: The reputation of the enrichment data.

short_desc.caption: Short Description
short_desc.description: A short description of the enrichment data.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The URL of the source of the enrichment data.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The enrichment type. For example: location.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the attribute to which the enriched data pertains.

enrichment.caption: Enrichment
enrichment.description: The Enrichment object provides inline enrichment data for specific attributes of interest within an event. It serves as a mechanism to enhance or supplement the information associated with the event by adding additional relevant details or context.
enrichment.name: enrichment

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the environment variable.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the environment variable.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the EPSS score was calculated.

percentile.caption: EPSS Percentile
percentile.description: The EPSS score's percentile representing relative importance and ranking of the score in the larger EPSS dataset.

score.caption: EPPS Score
score.description: The EPSS score representing the probability [0-1] of exploitation in the wild in the next 30 days (following score publication).

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the EPSS model used to calculate the score.

epss.caption: EPSS
epss.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) object describes the estimated probability a vulnerability will be exploited. EPSS is a community-driven effort to combine descriptive information about vulnerabilities (CVEs) with evidence of actual exploitation in-the-wild.
epss.name: epss

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: Describes details about the user/role/process that was the source of the activity that triggered the detection.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: Describes details about an AI agent associated with the activity that triggered the detection, whether the agent performed the activity, was its target, or was otherwise involved. Use a separate evidences entry per agent when a finding involves more than one, such as an agent spawning a sub-agent in violation of usage policy.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about the API call associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

connection_info.caption: Connection Info
connection_info.description: Describes details about the network connection associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

container.caption: Container
container.description: Describes details about the container associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional evidence data that is not accounted for in the specific evidence attributes. Use only when absolutely necessary.

database.caption: Database
database.description: Describes details about the database associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

databucket.caption: Databucket
databucket.description: Describes details about the databucket associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

device.caption: Device
device.description: An addressable device, computer system or host associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

dst_endpoint.caption: Destination Endpoint
dst_endpoint.description: Describes details about the destination of the network activity that triggered the detection.

email.caption: Email
email.description: The email object associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

file.caption: File
file.description: Describes details about the file associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

http_request.caption: HTTP Request
http_request.description: Describes details about the http request associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

http_response.caption: HTTP Response
http_response.description: Describes details about the http response associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

ja4_fingerprint_list.caption: JA4+ Fingerprints
ja4_fingerprint_list.description: Describes details about the JA4+ fingerprints that triggered the detection.

job.caption: Job
job.description: Describes details about the scheduled job that was associated with the activity that triggered the detection.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The naming convention or type identifier of the evidence associated with the security detection. For example, the @odata.type from Microsoft Graph Alerts V2 or display_name from CrowdStrike Falcon Incident Behaviors.

process.caption: Process
process.description: Describes details about the process associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

query.caption: DNS Query
query.description: Describes details about the DNS query associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

reg_key.caption: Registry Key
reg_key.description: Describes details about the registry key that triggered the detection.

reg_value.caption: Registry Value
reg_value.description: Describes details about the registry value that triggered the detection.

resources.caption: Cloud Resources
resources.description: Describes details about the cloud resources directly related to activity that triggered the detection. For resources impacted by the detection, use Affected Resources at the top-level of the finding.

script.caption: Script
script.description: Describes details about the script that was associated with the activity that triggered the detection.

src_endpoint.caption: Source Endpoint
src_endpoint.description: Describes details about the source of the network activity that triggered the detection.

tls.caption: TLS
tls.description: Describes details about the Transport Layer Security (TLS) activity that triggered the detection.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the evidence associated with the security detection. For example, the activity_id from CrowdStrike Falcon Alerts or behavior_id from CrowdStrike Falcon Incident Behaviors.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url.caption: URL
url.description: The URL object that pertains to the event or object associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

user.caption: User
user.description: Describes details about the user that was the target or somehow else associated with the activity that triggered the detection.

verdict.caption: Verdict
verdict.description: The normalized verdict of the evidence associated with the security detection.

verdict_id.caption: Verdict ID
verdict_id.description: The normalized verdict (or status) ID of the evidence associated with the security detection. For example, Microsoft Graph Security Alerts contain a verdict enumeration for each type of evidence associated with the Alert. This is typically set by an automated investigation process or an analyst/investigator assigned to the finding.

1.caption: False Positive
1.description: The verdict for the evidence has been identified as a False Positive.

10.caption: Duplicate
10.description: This evidence duplicates existing evidence related to this finding.

2.caption: True Positive
2.description: The verdict for the evidence has been identified as a True Positive.

3.caption: Disregard
3.description: The verdict for the evidence is that is should be Disregarded.

4.caption: Suspicious
4.description: The verdict for the evidence is that the behavior has been identified as Suspicious.

5.caption: Benign
5.description: The verdict for the evidence is that the behavior has been identified as Benign.

6.caption: Test
6.description: The evidence is part of a Test, or other sanctioned behavior(s).

7.caption: Insufficient Data
7.description: There is insufficient data to render a verdict on the evidence.

8.caption: Security Risk
8.description: The verdict for the evidence is that the behavior has been identified as a Security Risk.

9.caption: Managed Externally
9.description: The verdict for the evidence is Managed Externally, such as in a case management tool.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

win_service.caption: Windows Service
win_service.description: Describes details about the Windows service that triggered the detection.

evidences.caption: Evidence Artifacts
evidences.description: A collection of evidence artifacts associated to the activity/activities that triggered a security detection.
evidences.name: evidences

name.caption: Name
name.description: The schema extension name. For example: dev.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The schema extension unique identifier. For example: 999.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The schema extension version. For example: 1.0.0-alpha.2.

extension.caption: Schema Extension
extension.description: The OCSF Schema Extension object provides detailed information about the schema extension used to construct the event. The schema extensions are registered in the extensions.md file.
extension.name: extension

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the feature.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the feature.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

feature.caption: Feature
feature.description: The Feature object provides information about the software product feature that generated a specific event. It encompasses details related to the capabilities, components, user interface (UI) design, and performance upgrades associated with the feature.
feature.name: feature

accessed_time.caption: Accessed Time
accessed_time.description: The time when the file was last accessed.

accessor.caption: Accessor
accessor.description: The name of the user who last accessed the object.

attributes.caption: Attributes
attributes.description: The bitmask value that represents the file attributes.

company_name.caption: Company Name
company_name.description: The name of the company that published the file. For example: Microsoft Corporation.

confidentiality.caption: Confidentiality
confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidentiality_id.caption: Confidentiality ID
confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidentiality is not mapped. See the confidentiality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the file was created.

creator.caption: Creator
creator.description: The user that created the file.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the file, as returned by file system. For example: the description as returned by the Unix file command or the Windows file type.

download_info.caption: Download Info
download_info.description: Information pertaining to a downloaded file.

drive_type.caption: Drive Type
drive_type.description: The drive type, normalized to the caption of the drive_type_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

drive_type_id.caption: Drive Type ID
drive_type_id.description: Identifies the type of a disk drive, i.e. fixed, removable, etc.

1.caption: Removable
1.description: The drive has removable media; for example, a floppy drive, thumb drive, or flash card reader.

2.caption: Fixed
2.description: The drive has fixed media; for example, a hard disk drive or flash drive.

3.caption: Remote
3.description: The drive is a remote (network) drive.

4.caption: CD-ROM
4.description: The drive is a CD-ROM drive.

5.caption: RAM Disk
5.description: The drive is a RAM disk.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The drive type is not mapped. See the drive_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

encryption_details.caption: Encryption Details
encryption_details.description: The encryption details of the file. Should be populated if the file is encrypted.

ext.caption: File Extension
ext.description: The extension of the file, excluding the leading dot. For example: exe from svchost.exe, or gz from export.tar.gz.

imported_symbols.caption: Imported Symbols
imported_symbols.description: A list of symbols imported by the executable file.

internal_name.caption: Internal Name
internal_name.description: The name of the file as identified within the file itself. This contrasts with the name by which the file is known on disk. Where available, the internal name is widely used by security practitioners and detection content because the on-disk file name is not reliable. On the Windows OS, most PE files contain a VERSIONINFO resource from which the internal name can be obtained. On macOS, binaries can optionally embed a copy of the application's Info.plist file which in turn contains the name of the executable.

is_deleted.caption: Deleted
is_deleted.description: Indicates if the file was deleted from the filesystem.

is_encrypted.caption: Encrypted
is_encrypted.description: Indicates if the file is encrypted.

is_readonly.caption: Read-Only
is_readonly.description: Indicates that the file cannot be modified.

is_system.caption: System
is_system.description: The indication of whether the object is part of the operating system.

mime_type.caption: MIME type
mime_type.description: The Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) type of the file, if applicable.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the file was last modified.

modifier.caption: Modifier
modifier.description: The user that last modified the file.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the file. For example: svchost.exe

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The user that owns the file/object.

parent_folder.caption: Parent Folder
parent_folder.description: The parent folder in which the file resides. For example: c:\windows\system32

path.caption: Path
path.description: The full path to the file. For example: c:\windows\system32\svchost.exe.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product that created or installed the file.

signature.caption: Digital Signature
signature.description: The digital signature of the file.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of data, in bytes.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the file.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The file type.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The file type ID. Note the distinction between a Regular File and an Executable File. If the distinction is not known, or not indicated by the log, use Regular File. In this case, it should not be assumed that a Regular File is not executable.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the file as defined by the storage system, such the file system file ID.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

uri.caption: File URI
uri.description: The file URI, such as those reporting by static analysis tools. E.g., file:///C:/dev/sarif/sarif-tutorials/samples/Introduction/simple-example.js

url.caption: URL
url.description: The URL of the file, when applicable.

volume.caption: Volume
volume.description: The volume on the storage device where the file is located.

xattributes.caption: Extended Attributes
xattributes.description:
An unordered collection of zero or more name/value pairs where each pair represents a file or folder extended attribute.

For example: Windows alternate data stream attributes (ADS stream name, ADS size, etc.), user-defined or application-defined attributes, ACL, owner, primary group, etc. Examples from DCS:

  • ads_name
  • ads_size
  • dacl
  • owner
  • primary_group
  • link_name - name of the link associated to the file.
  • hard_link_count - the number of links that are associated to the file.

file.caption: File
file.description: The File object represents the metadata associated with a file stored in a computer system. It encompasses information about the file itself, including its attributes, properties, and organizational details.
file.name: file

analytic.caption: Analytic
analytic.description: The analytic technique used to analyze and derive insights from the data or information that led to the finding or conclusion.

attack_graph.caption: Attack Graph
attack_graph.description: An Attack Graph describes possible routes an attacker could take through an environment. It describes relationships between resources and their findings, such as malware detections, vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and other security actions.

references.description: MS Defender description of Attack Path

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of attack objects, each describing a tactic, technique, and/or sub-technique associated with the finding.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the finding was created.

data_sources.caption: Data Sources
data_sources.description: A list of data sources utilized in generation of the finding.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the reported finding.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description:
The time when the finding was first observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was first observed.

It can differ from the created_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was created.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: The Kill Chain provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description:
The time when the finding was most recently observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was most recently observed.

It can differ from the modified_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was last modified.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the finding was last modified.

product.caption: Product
product.description: Details about the product that reported the finding.

product_uid.caption: Product Identifier
product_uid.description: The unique identifier of the product that reported the finding.

related_analytics.caption: Related Analytics
related_analytics.description: Other analytics related to this finding.

related_events.caption: Related Events/Findings
related_events.description: Describes events and/or other findings related to the finding as identified by the security product. Note that these events may or may not be in OCSF.

related_events_count.caption: Related Events/Findings Count
related_events_count.description: Number of related events or findings.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The URL pointing to the source of the finding.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated with the finding.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the reported finding.

traits.caption: Traits
traits.description: The list of key traits or characteristics extracted from the finding.

types.caption: Types
types.description: One or more types of the reported finding.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the reported finding.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the reported finding.

finding_info.caption: Finding Information
finding_info.description: The Finding Information object describes metadata related to a security finding generated by a security tool or system.
finding_info.name: finding_info

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The algorithm or scheme used to create the fingerprint, normalized to the caption of algorithm_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

algorithm_id.caption: Algorithm ID
algorithm_id.description: The identifier of the normalized algorithm or scheme, which was used to create the fingerprint.

1.caption: MD5
1.description: MD5 message-digest algorithm producing a 128-bit (16-byte) hash value.

10.caption: SHA-512/224
10.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 512-bit (64-byte) hash value truncated to a 224-bit (28-byte) hash value.

11.caption: SHA-512/256
11.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 512-bit (64-byte) hash value truncated to a 256-bit (32-byte) hash value.

12.caption: SHA3-224
12.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 3 producing a 224-bit (28-byte) hash value.

13.caption: SHA3-256
13.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 3 producing a 256-bit (32-byte) hash value.

14.caption: SHA3-384
14.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 3 producing a 384-bit (48-byte) hash value.

15.caption: SHA3-512
15.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 3 producing a 512-bit (64-byte) hash value.

16.caption: xxHash H3 64-bit
16.description: xxHash H3 producing a 64-bit hash value.

17.caption: xxHash H3 128-bit
17.description: xxHash H3 producing a 128-bit hash value.

18.caption: Imphash
18.description: Import hash (imphash) based on the import table of a Portable Executable (PE) file producing a 128-bit (16-byte) hash value.

19.caption: NPF
19.description: Network Protocol Fingerprint (NPF) used to identify network protocols and applications.

2.caption: SHA-1
2.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 1 producing a 160-bit (20-byte) hash value.

20.caption: HASSH
20.description: HASSH is a network fingerprinting standard which can be used to identify specific SSH client and server implementations.

3.caption: SHA-256
3.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 256-bit (32-byte) hash value.

4.caption: SHA-512
4.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 512-bit (64-byte) hash value.

5.caption: CTPH
5.description: The ssdeep generated fuzzy checksum. Also known as Context Triggered Piecewise Hash (CTPH).

6.caption: TLSH
6.description: The TLSH fuzzy hashing algorithm.

7.caption: quickXorHash
7.description: Microsoft simple non-cryptographic hash algorithm that works by XORing the bytes in a circular-shifting fashion.

8.caption: SHA-224
8.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 224-bit (28-byte) hash value.

9.caption: SHA-384
9.description: Secure Hash Algorithm 2 producing a 384-bit (48-byte) hash value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The algorithm is not mapped. See the algorithm attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

encoding.caption: Encoding
encoding.description: The encoding of the value attribute, normalized to the caption of encoding_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

encoding_id.caption: Encoding ID
encoding_id.description: The normalized identifier of the encoding used to represent the fingerprint bytes as the string in value. A verifier must decode value using this encoding to recover the raw hash bytes.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The encoding of the fingerprint value is not known.

1.caption: Hex
1.description: The fingerprint value is encoded as a lowercase or uppercase hexadecimal string.

2.caption: Base64
2.description: The fingerprint value is encoded using standard Base64.

3.caption: Base64URL
3.description: The fingerprint value is encoded using URL- and filename-safe Base64.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The encoding of the fingerprint value is not mapped. See the encoding attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

serialization.caption: Serialization
serialization.description: The canonical serialization scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was fingerprinted, normalized to the caption of serialization_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

serialization_id.caption: Serialization ID
serialization_id.description: The identifier of the normalized canonical serialization scheme used to produce the deterministic byte sequence that was fingerprinted. A verifier must apply the same scheme to reproduce the fingerprinted input. Use Flat where the fingerprinted data is an opaque byte sequence, such as file content, to which no canonical serialization was applied. Distinct from algorithm_id, which identifies how the resulting bytes were hashed.

1.caption: Flat
1.description: No canonical serialization was applied; the fingerprint is computed over the data's raw byte sequence, such as the content of a disk file or any other opaque byte stream.

2.caption: JCS
2.description: JSON Canonicalization Scheme - deterministic JSON serialization of the structured data prior to hashing.

3.caption: JWS
3.description: JSON Web Signature - the JWS Signing Input, i.e. BASE64URL(protected header) '.' BASE64URL(payload).

4.caption: COSE
4.description: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption - the CBOR Sig_structure used as the binary input.

5.caption: DSSE
5.description: Dead Simple Signing Envelope - the PAE (Pre-Authentication Encoding) canonical input. Note: DSSE is a signing-envelope scheme, not a hash algorithm; the hash algorithm is carried in algorithm_id.

6.caption: Authenticode
6.description: The Portable Executable (PE) Image Hash procedure that canonicalizes the PE structure into the byte sequence fed to the digest, excluding specified header fields and digesting sections in a defined order.

references.description: Windows Authenticode Portable Executable Signature Format (Microsoft, 2008)

7.caption: Code Signing
7.description: The procedure that describes how hashes of code and other structures form the Code Directory message that is digested.

8.caption: App Package
8.description: The Windows Application Package signing procedure that describes how file hashes are stored in the manifest, and how that manifest is signed.

value.caption: Value
value.description:
The fingerprint value.

Note: This uses type file_hash_t ("Hash"), which has been generalized for all fingerprints but retains the same name and caption for backwards compatibility.

fingerprint.caption: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The Fingerprint object provides detailed information about a fingerprint, which is a compact representation of data used to identify a longer piece of information, such as a public key, file content, or application implementation. It contains the algorithm or scheme and value of the fingerprint, enabling efficient and reliable identification of the associated data.
fingerprint.name: fingerprint

condition.caption: Condition
condition.description: The rule trigger condition for the rule. For example: SQL_INJECTION.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the rule that generated the event.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The rule response time duration, usually used for challenge completion time.

match_details.caption: Match Details
match_details.description: The data in a request that rule matched. For example: '["10","and","1"]'.

match_location.caption: Match Location
match_location.description: The location of the matched data in the source which resulted in the triggered firewall rule. For example: HEADER.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the rule that generated the event.

rate_limit.caption: Rate Limit
rate_limit.description: The rate limit for a rate-based rule.

sensitivity.caption: Sensitivity
sensitivity.description: The sensitivity of the firewall rule in the matched event. For example: HIGH.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The rule type.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the rule that generated the event.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

firewall_rule.caption: Firewall Rule
firewall_rule.description: The Firewall Rule object represents a specific rule within a firewall policy or event. It contains information about a rule's configuration, properties, and associated actions that define how network traffic is handled by the firewall.
firewall_rule.name: firewall_rule

error.caption: Error Code
error.description: The error indication returned from the function. This may differ from the return value (e.g. when errno is used).

parameters.caption: Parameters
parameters.description: The parameters passed into a function invocation.

return_value.caption: Return Value
return_value.description: The value returned from a function.

function_invocation.caption: Function Invocation
function_invocation.description: The Function Invocation object provides details regarding the invocation of a function.
function_invocation.name: function_invocation

bus_type.caption: Bus Type
bus_type.description: The attachment bus or interface standard, normalized to the caption of the bus_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

bus_type_id.caption: Bus Type ID
bus_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the attachment bus or interface standard.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The bus type is unknown or not reported.

1.caption: Onboard
1.description: The device is attached directly on the motherboard or SoC (often referred to as 'integrated' or 'onboard').

2.caption: PCIe x16
2.description: Peripheral Component Interconnect Express slot with 16 lanes, typically used for high‑bandwidth add‑in devices.

3.caption: PCIe x8
3.description: Peripheral Component Interconnect Express slot with 8 lanes; common for high‑performance NICs, storage controllers, and accelerators.

4.caption: MXM Type A
4.description: Mobile PCI Express Module (MXM) Type A form factor (compact laptop/embedded GPU module).

5.caption: MXM Type B
5.description: Mobile PCI Express Module (MXM) Type B form factor (larger laptop/embedded GPU module).

6.caption: M.2
6.description: M.2 (NGFF) internal module form factor/connector exposing PCIe (and/or SATA/USB) for SSDs and add‑in modules.

7.caption: CXL
7.description: Compute Express Link (CXL), an open cache‑coherent interconnect for processors, memory expansion, and accelerators built on the PCIe physical layer.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A bus or interface standard not covered by the defined values; the exact value is reported by the event source.

cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The number of processing cores or compute units for the component.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the GPU. For example: GeForce RTX A6000, Radeon PRO W7900, or Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the GPU. For example: NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel.

vram_mode.caption: VRAM Mode
vram_mode.description: The video memory attachment mode, indicating how the VRAM hardware is integrated with the system (e.g., shared or dedicated), normalized to the caption of the vram_mode_id value. For 'Other', the exact attachment mode is defined by the event source.

vram_mode_id.caption: VRAM Mode ID
vram_mode_id.description: The normalized identifier of the video memory attachment mode.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The VRAM mode is unknown or not reported.

1.caption: Shared
1.description: Video memory is allocated from system memory.

2.caption: Dedicated
2.description: Video memory is physically separate from system memory.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A VRAM mode not covered by the defined values; the exact value is reported by the event source.

vram_size.caption: VRAM Size
vram_size.description: The total amount of installed video RAM.

gpu_info.caption: GPU Information
gpu_info.description: The GPU information object contains attributes describing graphical processing hardware.
gpu_info.name: gpu_info

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The graph description - provides additional details about the graph's purpose and contents.

edges.caption: Edges
edges.description: The edges/connections between nodes in the graph - contains the collection of edge objects defining relationships between nodes.

is_directed.caption: Directed
is_directed.description: Indicates if the graph is directed (true) or undirected (false).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The graph name - a human readable identifier for the graph.

nodes.caption: Nodes
nodes.description: The nodes/vertices of the graph - contains the collection of node objects that make up the graph.

query_language.caption: Query Language
query_language.description: The graph query language, normalized to the caption of the query_language_id value.

query_language_id.caption: Query Language ID
query_language_id.description: The normalized identifier of a graph query language that can be used to interact with the graph.

1.caption: Cypher
1.description: A declarative graph query language developed by Neo4j that allows for expressive and efficient querying of graph databases.

2.caption: GraphQL
2.description: A query language for APIs that enables declarative data fetching and provides a complete description of the data in the API.

3.caption: Gremlin
3.description: A graph traversal language and virtual machine developed by Apache TinkerPop that enables graph computing across different graph databases.

4.caption: GQL
4.description: An ISO standard graph query language designed to provide a unified way to query graph databases.

5.caption: G-CORE
5.description: A graph query language that combines features from existing languages while adding support for paths as first-class citizens.

6.caption: PGQL
6.description: Property Graph Query Language developed by Oracle that provides SQL-like syntax for querying property graphs.

7.caption: SPARQL
7.description: A semantic query language for databases that enables querying and manipulating data stored in RDF format.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The Query Language is not mapped. See the query_language attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The graph type. Typically useful to represent the specific type of graph that is used.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: Unique identifier of the graph - a unique ID to reference this specific graph.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

graph.caption: Graph
graph.description: A graph data structure representation with nodes and edges.
graph.name: graph

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The group description.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain where the group is defined. For example: the LDAP or Active Directory domain.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The group name.

type.caption: Group Type
type.description: The type of the group.
