uid.description: The unique identifier of the group. For example, for Windows events this is the security identifier (SID) of the group. Another example, pool id or desktop id that the device belongs to.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The Group object represents a collection or association of entities, such as users, policies, or devices. It serves as a logical grouping mechanism to organize and manage entities with similar characteristics or permissions within a system or organization, including but not limited to purposes of access control.
group.name: group

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain name for the server from which the http_cookie is served.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the HTTP cookie.

http_only.caption: HTTP Only
http_only.description: A cookie attribute to make it inaccessible via JavaScript

is_http_only.caption: HTTP Only
is_http_only.description: This attribute prevents the cookie from being accessed via JavaScript.

is_secure.caption: Secure
is_secure.description: The cookie attribute indicates that cookies are sent to the server only when the request is encrypted using the HTTPS protocol.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The HTTP cookie name.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The path of the HTTP cookie.

samesite.caption: SameSite
samesite.description: The cookie attribute that lets servers specify whether/when cookies are sent with cross-site requests. Values are: Strict, Lax or None

secure.caption: Secure
secure.description: The cookie attribute to only send cookies to the server with an encrypted request over the HTTPS protocol.

http_cookie.caption: HTTP Cookie
http_cookie.description: The HTTP Cookie object, also known as a web cookie or browser cookie, contains details and values pertaining to a small piece of data that a server sends to a user's web browser. This data is then stored by the browser and sent back to the server with subsequent requests, allowing the server to remember and track certain information about the user's browsing session or preferences.
http_cookie.name: http_cookie

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the HTTP header.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the HTTP header.

http_header.caption: HTTP Header
http_header.description: The HTTP Header object represents the headers sent in an HTTP request or response. HTTP headers are key-value pairs that convey additional information about the HTTP message, including details about the content, caching, authentication, encoding, and other aspects of the communication.
http_header.name: http_header

args.caption: HTTP Arguments
args.description: The arguments sent along with the HTTP request.

body_length.caption: Request Body Length
body_length.description: The actual length of the HTTP request body, in number of bytes, independent of a potentially existing Content-Length header.

http_headers.caption: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

http_method.caption: HTTP Method
http_method.description: The HTTP request method indicates the desired action to be performed for a given resource.

ACL.caption: ACL
ACL.description: The ACL method modifies the access control list of the specified resource.

BASELINE-CONTROL.caption: Baseline Control
BASELINE-CONTROL.description: The BASELINE-CONTROL method places the specified collection resource under baseline control.

BIND.caption: Bind
BIND.description: The BIND method adds a binding to the specified collection resource.

CHECKIN.caption: Check In
CHECKIN.description: The CHECKIN method creates a new version from a checked-out version-controlled resource.

CHECKOUT.caption: Check Out
CHECKOUT.description: The CHECKOUT method prepares a version-controlled resource for modification.

CONNECT.caption: Connect
CONNECT.description: The CONNECT method establishes a tunnel to the server identified by the target resource.

COPY.caption: Copy
COPY.description: The COPY method duplicates the specified resource.

DELETE.caption: Delete
DELETE.description: The DELETE method deletes the specified resource.

GET.caption: Get
GET.description: The GET method requests a representation of the specified resource. Requests using GET should only retrieve data.

HEAD.caption: Head
HEAD.description: The HEAD method asks for a response identical to a GET request, but without the response body.

LABEL.caption: Label
LABEL.description: The LABEL method adds, sets, or removes labels on a version-controlled resource.

LINK.caption: Link
LINK.description: The LINK method establishes one or more links between resources.

LOCK.caption: Lock
LOCK.description: The LOCK method acquires or refreshes a lock on the specified resource.

MERGE.caption: Merge
MERGE.description: The MERGE method merges changes from another resource into the specified resource.

MKACTIVITY.caption: Make Activity
MKACTIVITY.description: The MKACTIVITY method creates a new activity resource.

MKCALENDAR.caption: Make Calendar
MKCALENDAR.description: The MKCALENDAR method creates a new calendar collection resource.

MKCOL.caption: Make Collection
MKCOL.description: The MKCOL method creates a new collection resource.

MKREDIRECTREF.caption: Make Redirect Reference
MKREDIRECTREF.description: The MKREDIRECTREF method creates a new redirect reference resource.

MKWORKSPACE.caption: Make Workspace
MKWORKSPACE.description: The MKWORKSPACE method creates a new workspace resource.

MOVE.caption: Move
MOVE.description: The MOVE method atomically duplicates and deletes the specified resource.

OPTIONS.caption: Options
OPTIONS.description: The OPTIONS method describes the communication options for the target resource.

ORDERPATCH.caption: Order Patch
ORDERPATCH.description: The ORDERPATCH method changes the ordering of members in an ordered collection.

PATCH.caption: Patch
PATCH.description: The PATCH method applies partial modifications to a resource.

POST.caption: Post
POST.description: The POST method submits an entity to the specified resource, often causing a change in state or side effects on the server.

PRI.caption: PRI
PRI.description: The PRI method appears in the HTTP/2 connection preface to confirm the protocol.

PROPFIND.caption: Property Find
PROPFIND.description: The PROPFIND method retrieves properties defined on the specified resource.

PROPPATCH.caption: Property Patch
PROPPATCH.description: The PROPPATCH method sets and/or removes properties defined on the specified resource.

PUT.caption: Put
PUT.description: The PUT method replaces all current representations of the target resource with the request payload.

QUERY.caption: Query
QUERY.description: The QUERY method performs a safe query request that can include a request body.

REBIND.caption: Rebind
REBIND.description: The REBIND method moves a binding from one collection to another.

REPORT.caption: Report
REPORT.description: The REPORT method retrieves a report about the specified resource.

SEARCH.caption: Search
SEARCH.description: The SEARCH method searches a resource or collection using the request payload.

TRACE.caption: Trace
TRACE.description: The TRACE method performs a message loop-back test along the path to the target resource.

UNBIND.caption: Unbind
UNBIND.description: The UNBIND method removes a binding from the specified collection resource.

UNCHECKOUT.caption: Un-Check Out
UNCHECKOUT.description: The UNCHECKOUT method cancels a checkout and restores the resource to its previous state.

UNLINK.caption: Unlink
UNLINK.description: The UNLINK method removes one or more links between resources.

UNLOCK.caption: Unlock
UNLOCK.description: The UNLOCK method releases a lock on the specified resource.

UPDATE.caption: Update
UPDATE.description: The UPDATE method updates a version-controlled resource to match a specified version.

UPDATEREDIRECTREF.caption: Update Redirect Reference
UPDATEREDIRECTREF.description: The UPDATEREDIRECTREF method changes the target of a redirect reference resource.

VERSION-CONTROL.caption: Version Control
VERSION-CONTROL.description: The VERSION-CONTROL method places the specified resource under version control.

length.caption: Request Length
length.description: The length of the entire HTTP request, in number of bytes.

referrer.caption: HTTP Referrer
referrer.description: The request header that identifies the address of the previous web page, which is linked to the current web page or resource being requested.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the http request.

url.caption: URL
url.description: The URL object that pertains to the request.

user_agent.caption: HTTP User-Agent
user_agent.description: The request header that identifies the operating system and web browser.

x_forwarded_for.caption: X-Forwarded-For
x_forwarded_for.description: The X-Forwarded-For header identifying the originating IP address(es) of a client connecting to a web server through an HTTP proxy or a load balancer.

http_request.caption: HTTP Request
http_request.description: The HTTP Request object represents the attributes of a request made to a web server. It encapsulates the details and metadata associated with an HTTP request, including the request method, headers, URL, query parameters, body content, and other relevant information.
http_request.name: http_request

body_length.caption: Response Body Length
body_length.description: The actual length of the HTTP response body, in number of bytes, independent of a potentially existing Content-Length header.

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) status code returned from the web server to the client. For example, 200.

content_type.caption: HTTP Content Type
content_type.description: The HTTP request header that identifies the original media type of the resource (prior to any content encoding applied for sending).

http_headers.caption: HTTP Headers
http_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers of an HTTP request or response.

latency.caption: Latency
latency.description: The HTTP response latency measured in milliseconds.

length.caption: Response Length
length.description: The length of the entire HTTP response, in number of bytes.

@deprecated.message: Redundant with the code and status attributes, which together convey the HTTP status code and its reason phrase. Use code for the numeric value and status for the human-readable label.

message.caption: Message
message.description: The HTTP status code and reason phrase returned from the server.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The response status. For example: A successful HTTP status of 'OK' which corresponds to a code of 200.

http_response.caption: HTTP Response
http_response.description: The HTTP Response object contains detailed information about the response sent from a web server to the requester. It encompasses attributes and metadata that describe the response status, headers, body content, and other relevant information.
http_response.name: http_response

account.caption: Account
account.description: The account associated with the role. For example, can be a cross-account role, different from the user or group account, granting access within this account.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The role name. For example, Power Users.

policies.caption: Policies
policies.description: IAM policies associated with the role.

privileges.caption: Privileges
privileges.description: List of privileges assigned to a role.

programmatic_credentials.caption: Programmatic Credentials
programmatic_credentials.description: Programmatic credential (API keys, access tokens, certificates, etc) associated with the role.

resources.caption: Resources Array
resources.description: Resources that the role applies to.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The session where the role is active. Some roles may be temporary and expire when the session expires.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique role identifier. For example, the Windows role SID, or AWS role ARN.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternate user identifier. For example, the Active Directory role GUID or the associated LDAP group DN.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

iam_role.caption: IAM Role
iam_role.description: The IAM Role object describes permission characteristics (or privileges) associated with a user or group of users as security principals against one or more resources. In some cases only the name or ID of the role is known hence other attributes are optional. In some systems a user or group of users can have multiple roles, imparting the union of privileges to the principal. In some systems the role can serve as a temporary security principal without its own credentials on behalf of the actual security principal.
iam_role.name: iam_role

auth_factors.caption: Authentication Factors
auth_factors.description: The Authentication Factors object describes the different types of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) methods and/or devices supported by the Identity Provider.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The primary domain associated with the Identity Provider.

fingerprint.caption: Certificate Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the X.509 certificate used by the Identity Provider.

has_mfa.caption: MFA Enforced
has_mfa.description: The Identity Provider enforces Multi Factor Authentication (MFA).

issuer.caption: Issuer Details
issuer.description: The unique identifier (often a URL) used by the Identity Provider as its issuer.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the Identity Provider.

protocol_name.caption: Supported Protocol
protocol_name.description: The supported protocol of the Identity Provider. E.g., SAML, OIDC, or OAuth2.

scim.caption: SCIM
scim.description: The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) resource object as defined in RFC 7634 provides a structured set of attributes related to SCIM protocols used for identity provisioning and management across cloud-based platforms. It standardizes user and group provisioning details, enabling identity synchronization and lifecycle management with compatible Identity Providers (IdPs) and applications.

sso.caption: SSO
sso.description: The Single Sign-On (SSO) object provides a structure for normalizing SSO attributes, configuration, and/or settings from Identity Providers.

state.caption: State
state.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider, normalized to the caption of the state_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

state_id.caption: State ID
state_id.description: The normalized state ID of the Identity Provider to reflect its configuration or activation status.

0.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider is unknown.

1.caption: Active
1.description: The Identity Provider is in an Active state, or otherwise enabled.

2.caption: Suspended
2.description: The Identity Provider is in a Suspended state.

3.caption: Deprecated
3.description: The Identity Provider is in a Deprecated state, or is otherwise disabled.

4.caption: Deleted
4.description: The Identity Provider is in a Deleted state.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

tenant_uid.caption: Tenant UID
tenant_uid.description: The tenant ID associated with the Identity Provider.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the Identity Provider.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url_string.caption: Configuration URL
url_string.description: The URL for accessing the configuration or metadata of the Identity Provider.

idp.caption: Identity Provider
idp.description: The Identity Provider object contains detailed information about a provider responsible for creating, maintaining, and managing identity information while offering authentication services to applications. An Identity Provider (IdP) serves as a trusted authority that verifies the identity of users and issues authentication tokens or assertions to enable secure access to applications or services.
idp.name: idp

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the image.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The image name. For example: elixir.

path.description: The full path to the image file.

tags.caption: Tags

4.description: The job is executed by launchd on macOS.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The job orchestration mechanism is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique job identifier.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that created the job.

job.caption: Job
job.description: The Job object provides information about a scheduled job or task, including its name, command line, and state. It encompasses attributes that describe the properties and status of the scheduled job.
job.name: job

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description:
When type_id is Execute (2), this describes the command line that is executed.

When type_id is COM Handler (1), this may describe the DLL path stored in the COM component's InprocServer32 key or the command line stored in the COM component's LocalServer32 key.

com_class_uuid.caption: COM Class Identifier
com_class_uuid.description: When type_id is COM Handler (1), this describes the COM Class Identifier (CLSID).

file.caption: File
file.description: When known, describes the image file that is executed when type_id is COM Handler or Execute. Note that this attribute is intended to supplement the com_class_uid or cmd_line attributes, and is not an alternative to them.

properties.caption: Properties
properties.description:
The list of properties associated with the performed action.
Can be populated with additional attributes of a program execution process, COM object attributes, fields of a message box or an email.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The job action type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

1.caption: COM Handler
1.description: The action fires a COM handler. When this type is used, com_class_uuid and file attributes may be populated.

2.caption: Execute
2.description: The action executes a command-line operation. When this type is used, cmd_line and file attributes may be populated.

3.caption: E-mail
3.description: The action sends an email.

4.caption: Show Message
4.description: The action shows a message box with specified message and title.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The performed action is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

working_directory.caption: Working Directory
working_directory.description: When type_id is Execute (2), this describes the working directory of a program that is run by the job.

job_action.caption: Job Action
job_action.description: The action that will be performed by the job when certain conditions are met.
job_action.name: job_action

event_codes.caption: Event Codes
event_codes.description: Event identifiers that pertain to the job trigger. Should be populated when the Event (3) type is specified.

last_run_time.caption: Last Run
last_run_time.description: The time when the job was last run.

log_sources.caption: Log Sources
log_sources.description: A collection of log systems or components that pertain to the job trigger. Should be populated when the Event (3) type is specified.

next_run_time.caption: Next Run
next_run_time.description: The time when the job will next be run.

properties.caption: Properties
properties.description:
The list of properties associated with the trigger.
Can be used to describe time boundaries of the job, amount of repetitions or when the job should be activated or expired.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The job trigger type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The job trigger type, i.e. the condition that must be met for the job to perform its action.

1.caption: Boot
1.description: The job is triggered on a system boot.

2.caption: Schedule
2.description: The job is triggered on a specific schedule. Properties should be populated with respective time bounds.

3.caption: Event
3.description: The job is triggered when the specific event occurs. The properties attribute should be populated with respective event sources and identifiers.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The job trigger is unmapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that pertains to the job trigger. Can be populated when the Event (3) type that bounds to specific user is used.

job_trigger.caption: Job Trigger
job_trigger.description: The condition or event that, when met, will initiate the job to perform specified actions.
job_trigger.name: job_trigger

classification.caption: Classification
classification.description: The vendors classification of the kb article.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The date the kb article was released by the vendor.

install_state.caption: Install State
install_state.description: The install state of the kb article.

install_state_id.caption: Install State ID
install_state_id.description: The normalized install state ID of the kb article.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The normalized install state is unknown.

1.caption: Installed
1.description: The item is installed.

2.caption: Not Installed
2.description: The item is not installed.

3.caption: Installed Pending Reboot
3.description: The item is installed pending reboot operation.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The install state is not mapped. See the install_state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

is_superseded.caption: The patch is superseded.
is_superseded.description: The kb article has been replaced by another.

os.caption: OS
os.description: The operating system the kb article applies.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product details the kb article applies.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The severity of the kb article.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes for the kb article.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The kb article link from the source vendor.

title.caption: Title
title.description: The title of the kb article.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the kb article.

kb_article.caption: KB Article
kb_article.description: The KB Article object contains metadata that describes the patch or update.
kb_article.name: kb_article

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the key.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value associated to the key.

values.caption: Values
values.description: Optional, the values associated to the key. You can populate this attribute, when you have multiple values for the same key.

key_value_object.caption: Key:Value object
key_value_object.description: A generic object allowing to define a {key:value} pair.
key_value_object.name: key_value_object

function_keys.caption: Function Keys
function_keys.description: The number of function keys on client keyboard.

ime.caption: IME
ime.description: The Input Method Editor (IME) file name.

keyboard_layout.caption: Keyboard Layout
keyboard_layout.description: The keyboard locale identifier name (e.g., en-US).

keyboard_info.caption: Keyboard Information
keyboard_info.description: The Keyboard Information object contains details and attributes related to a computer or device keyboard. It encompasses information that describes the characteristics, capabilities, and configuration of the keyboard.
keyboard_info.name: keyboard_info

phase_id.caption: Kill Chain Phase ID
phase_id.description: The cyber kill chain phase identifier.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The kill chain phase is unknown.

1.caption: Reconnaissance
1.description: The attackers pick a target and perform a detailed analysis, start collecting information (email addresses, conferences information, etc.) and evaluate the victim’s vulnerabilities to determine how to exploit them.

2.caption: Weaponization
2.description: The attackers develop a malware weapon and aim to exploit the discovered vulnerabilities.

3.caption: Delivery
3.description: The intruders will use various tactics, such as phishing, infected USB drives, etc.

4.caption: Exploitation
4.description: The intruders start leveraging vulnerabilities to executed code on the victim’s system.

5.caption: Installation
5.description: The intruders install malware on the victim’s system.

6.caption: Command & Control
6.description: Malware opens a command channel to enable the intruders to remotely manipulate the victim's system.

7.caption: Actions on Objectives
7.description: With hands-on keyboard access, intruders accomplish the mission’s goal.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The kill chain phase is not mapped. See the phase attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

kill_chain_phase.caption: Kill Chain Phase
kill_chain_phase.description: The Kill Chain Phase object represents a single phase of a cyber attack, including the initial reconnaissance and planning stages up to the final objective of the attacker. It provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.
kill_chain_phase.name: kill_chain_phase

cost_center.caption: Cost Center
cost_center.description: The cost center associated with the user.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp when the user was created.

deleted_time.caption: Deleted Time
deleted_time.description: The timestamp when the user was deleted. In Active Directory (AD), when a user is deleted they are moved to a temporary container and then removed after 30 days. So, this field can be populated even after a user is deleted for the next 30 days.

department.caption: Department
department.description: The name of the department in which the user works.

display_name.caption: Display Name
display_name.description: The display name of the LDAP person. According to RFC 2798, this is the preferred name of a person to be used when displaying entries.

email_addrs.caption: Email Addresses
email_addrs.description: A list of additional email addresses for the user.

employee_uid.caption: Employee ID
employee_uid.description: The employee identifier assigned to the user by the organization.

given_name.caption: Given Name
given_name.description: The given or first name of the user.

hire_time.caption: Hire Time
hire_time.description: The timestamp when the user was or will be hired by the organization.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The labels associated with the user. For example in AD this could be the userType, employeeType. For example: Member, Employee.

last_login_time.caption: Last Login
last_login_time.description: The last time when the user logged in.

ldap_cn.caption: LDAP Common Name
ldap_cn.description: The LDAP and X.500 commonName attribute, typically the full name of the person. For example, John Doe.

ldap_dn.caption: LDAP Distinguished Name
ldap_dn.description: The X.500 Distinguished Name (DN) is a structured string that uniquely identifies an entry, such as a user, in an X.500 directory service For example, cn=John Doe,ou=People,dc=example,dc=com.

leave_time.caption: Leave Time
leave_time.description: The timestamp when the user left or will be leaving the organization.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location associated with a user. This is typically the user's usual work location.

manager.caption: Manager
manager.description: The user's manager. This helps in understanding an org hierarchy. This should only ever be populated once in an event. I.e. there should not be a manager's manager in an event.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The timestamp when the user entry was last modified.

office_location.caption: Office Location
office_location.description: The primary office location associated with the user. This could be any string and isn't a specific address. For example, South East Virtual.

phone_number.caption: Telephone Number
phone_number.description: The telephone number of the user. Corresponds to the LDAP Telephone-Number CN.

surname.caption: Surname
surname.description: The last or family name for the user.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the user.

ldap_person.caption: LDAP Person
ldap_person.description: The additional LDAP attributes that describe a person.
ldap_person.name: ldap_person

aerial_height.caption: Aerial Height
aerial_height.description: Expressed as either height above takeoff location or height above ground level (AGL) for a UAS current location. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

coordinates.caption: Coordinates
coordinates.description: A two-element array, containing a longitude/latitude pair. The format conforms with GeoJSON. For example: [-73.983, 40.719].

country.caption: Country
country.description:
The ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code.

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the geographical location.

geodetic_altitude.caption: Geodetic Altitude
geodetic_altitude.description: The aircraft distance above or below the ellipsoid as measured along a line that passes through the aircraft and is normal to the surface of the WGS-84 ellipsoid. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

geodetic_vertical_accuracy.caption: Geodetic Vertical Accuracy
geodetic_vertical_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on geodetic altitude. This is based on ADS-B Geodetic Vertical Accuracy (GVA). Measured in meters.

geohash.caption: Geohash
geohash.description:
Geohash of the geo-coordinates (latitude and longitude).

Geohashing is a geocoding system used to encode geographic coordinates in decimal degrees, to a single string.

horizontal_accuracy.caption: Horizontal Accuracy
horizontal_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on horizontal position. This is based on ADS-B NACp. Measured in meters.

is_on_premises.caption: On-Premises
is_on_premises.description: Indicates whether the location is on-premises.

@deprecated.message: Use the network_endpoint.isp or whois.isp attribute according to your use-case.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

lat.caption: Latitude
lat.description: The geographical Latitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: 42.361145.

long.caption: Longitude
long.description: The geographical Longitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: -71.057083.

postal_code.caption: Postal Code
postal_code.description: The postal code of the location.

pressure_altitude.caption: Pressure Altitude
pressure_altitude.description: The uncorrected barometric pressure altitude (based on reference standard 29.92 inHg, 1013.25 mb) provides a reference for algorithms that utilize 'altitude deltas' between aircraft. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m.. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The provider of the geographical location data.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The alphanumeric code that identifies the principal subdivision (e.g. province or state) of the country. For example, 'CH-VD' for the Canton of Vaud, Switzerland

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The Geo Location object describes a geographical location, usually associated with an IP address.
location.name: location

device.caption: Device
device.description: The device where the events are logged.

event_uid.caption: Event UID
event_uid.description: The unique identifier of the event assigned by the logger.

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

log_format.caption: Log Format
log_format.description: The format of data in the log. For example JSON, syslog or CSV.

log_level.caption: Log Level
log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.caption: Log Name
log_name.description: The log name for the logging provider log, or the file name of the system log. This may be an intermediate store-and-forward log or a vendor destination log. For example /archive/server1/var/log/messages.0 or /var/log/.

log_provider.caption: Log Provider
log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. This may be an intermediate application store-and-forward log or a vendor destination log.

log_version.caption: Log Version
log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.caption: Logged Time
logged_time.description: The time when this logger received and logged the event. For the last logger in the pipeline, this value should match metadata.logged_time.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the logging product instance.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product logging the event.  This may be the event source product, a management server product, a scanning product, a SIEM, etc.

transmit_time.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the logging product instance.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the logging provider.

logger.caption: Logger
logger.description: The Logger object represents the device and product where events are stored with times for receipt and transmission.  This may be at the source device where the event occurred, a remote scanning device, intermediate hops, or the ultimate destination.
logger.name: logger

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates that value has been truncated. May be omitted if truncation has not occurred.

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The size in bytes of the string represented by value before truncation. Should be omitted if truncation has not occurred.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The string value, truncated if is_truncated is true.

long_string.caption: Long String
long_string.description: This object is a used to capture strings which may be truncated by a security product due to their length.
long_string.name: long_string

classification_ids.caption: Classification IDs
classification_ids.description: The list of normalized identifiers of the malware classifications.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The classification is not mapped. See the classifications attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

classifications.caption: Classifications
classifications.description: The list of malware classifications, normalized to the captions of the classification_ids values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

cves.caption: CVE List
cves.description: The list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers associated with the malware.

files.caption: Files
files.description: The list of file objects representing files that were identified as infected by the malware.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The malware name, as reported by the detection engine.

num_infected.caption: Number of Infected Entities
num_infected.description: The number of files that were identified to be infected by the malware.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The filesystem path of the malware that was observed.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The name or identifier of the security solution or service that provided the malware detection information.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The severity of the malware, normalized to the captions of the severity_id values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the malware severity.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the specific malware instance, as assigned by the detection engine (e.g., virus signature ID or IPS rule ID).

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: The Malware object describes the classification of known malicious software, which is intentionally designed to cause damage to a computer, server, client, or computer network.
malware.name: malware

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job completed execution.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The administrator-supplied or application-generated name of the scan. For example: "Home office weekly user database scan", "Scan folders for viruses", "Full system virus scan"

num_files.caption: Scanned Files
num_files.description: The total number of files analyzed during the scan.

num_infected.caption: Number of Infected Entities
num_infected.description: The total number of files identified as infected with malware during the scan.

num_volumes.caption: Number of Volumes
num_volumes.description: The total number of storage volumes examined during the malware scan.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The total size in bytes of all files that were scanned.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job began execution.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of scan.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type id of the scan.

1.caption: Manual
1.description: The scan was manually initiated by the user or administrator.

2.caption: Scheduled
2.description: The scan was started based on scheduler.

3.caption: Updated Content
3.description: The scan was triggered by a content update.

4.caption: Quarantined Items
4.description: The scan was triggered by newly quarantined items.

5.caption: Attached Media
5.description: The scan was triggered by the attachment of removable media.

6.caption: User Logon
6.description: The scan was started due to a user logon.

7.caption: ELAM
7.description: The scan was triggered by an Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) detection.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The scan type id is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Scan UID
uid.description: The application-defined unique identifier assigned to an instance of a scan.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

unique_malware_count.caption: Unique Malware Count
unique_malware_count.description: The number of unique malware detected across all infected files.

malware_scan_info.caption: Malware Scan Info
malware_scan_info.description: The malware scan information object describes characteristics, metadata of a malware scanning job.
malware_scan_info.name: malware_scan_info

ai_role_id.caption: AI Role ID
ai_role_id.description: Specifies the functional role of the AI within the context of this message, such as retrieving information, assisting reasoning, executing a tool, or generating content.

1.caption: User
1.description: The human user initiating a request.

2.caption: Assistant
2.description: The AI model generating a response.

3.caption: Tool
3.description: A callable tool or API invoked by the assistant.

4.caption: Agent
4.description: A software agent that performs tasks with autonomy or delegated intent.

5.caption: Orchestrator
5.description: The component coordinating multiple agents or tools.

6.caption: Retriever
6.description: A component that retrieves information or context from a knowledge source (e.g., vector DB, search system, or API).

99.caption: Other
99.description: Other role type not covered above.

application.caption: Application
application.description: The initiating client application. In AI systems, this represents the client-side application or framework that initiates requests (e.g., LangChain application, web browser, mobile app, SDK implementation).

completion_tokens.caption: Completion Tokens
completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the model's response/completion for this message.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name or identifier of the message context. In AI systems, this could be the conversation ID, session name, thread identifier, or interaction name (e.g., 'user-session-123', 'conversation-abc', 'chat-thread-456').

prompt_text.caption: Prompt Text
prompt_text.description: The text of the input prompt provided to the model for this message. This is the verbatim instruction, query, or context supplied to the AI system that drove the operation.

prompt_tokens.caption: Prompt Tokens
prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the input prompt for this message.

response_text.caption: Response Text
response_text.description: The text of the model's response generated for this message. For agent-mediated operations, this is the content returned by the assistant, tool, or agent.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The server or service handling the request. In AI systems, this represents the AI service, API endpoint, or agent that processes and responds to requests (e.g., OpenAI API service, Claude API service, internal AI model service).

total_tokens.caption: Total Tokens
total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens used for this message (prompt + completion).

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the message context. This could be a session ID, conversation ID, or other unique identifier that allows correlation of messages within the same context.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

message_context.caption: Message Context
message_context.description: Communication context for AI system interactions including protocols, roles, clients, and session information for MCP and other AI communication systems.
message_context.name: message_context

references.description: OWASP AI Security and Privacy Guide - Agent Security

correlation_uid.caption: Correlation UID
correlation_uid.description: A unique identifier used to correlate this OCSF event with other related OCSF events, distinct from the event's uid value. This enables linking multiple OCSF events that are part of the same activity, transaction, or security incident across different systems or time periods.

debug.caption: Debug Information
debug.description: Debug information about non-fatal issues with this OCSF event. Each issue is a line in this string array.

event_code.caption: Event Code
event_code.description: The identifier of the original event. For example the numerical Windows Event Code or Cisco syslog code.

extension.caption: Schema Extension
extension.description: The schema extension used to create the event.

extensions.caption: Schema Extensions
extensions.description: The schema extensions used to create the event.

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels attached to the event. For example: ["sample", "dev"]

log_format.caption: Log Source Format
log_format.description: The format of data in the log where the data originated. For example CSV, XML, Windows Multiline, JSON, syslog or Cisco Log Schema.

log_level.caption: Log Level
log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.caption: Log Name
log_name.description: The event log name, typically for the consumer of the event. For example, the storage bucket name, SIEM repository index name, etc.

log_provider.caption: Log Provider
log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. For example AWS CloudWatch or Splunk.

log_source.caption: Log Source
log_source.description: The log system or component where the data originated. For example, a file path, syslog server name or a Windows hostname and logging subsystem such as Security.

log_version.caption: Log Version
log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.caption: Logged Time
logged_time.description: The ultimate logged time in the event pipeline - when the event reached its final destination (e.g., SIEM, data lake). If loggers is populated, this should match the logged_time of the last entry in the loggers array. This is distinct from time (when the activity occurred) and processed_time (when an intermediate system processed the event).

loggers.caption: Loggers
loggers.description: An ordered array of Logger objects describing each hop in the event pipeline between the source and its final destination. Each entry captures the logging product, device, and timestamps (logged_time, transmit_time) at that stage. The last entry's logged_time should match metadata.logged_time.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

original_event_uid.caption: Original Event ID
original_event_uid.description: The unique identifier assigned to the event in its original logging system before transformation to OCSF format. This field preserves the source system's native event identifier, enabling traceability back to the raw log entry. For example, a Windows Event Record ID, a syslog message ID, a Splunk _cd value, or a database transaction log sequence number.

original_time.caption: Original Time
original_time.description: The original event time as reported by the event source, preserved as a pass-through string in its native format (e.g., Syslog timestamp, Windows event time). This is not normalized to timestamp_t - the normalized equivalent is the base event time attribute. Omit if the event is generated rather than collected via logs.

processed_time.caption: Processed Time
processed_time.description: The time when the event was processed by an intermediate system (e.g., ETL pipeline, event processor) before reaching its final destination. Can be used with logged_time to calculate queuing duration via total_queued_duration.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product that reported the event.

profiles.caption: Profiles
profiles.description: The list of profiles used to create the event. Profiles should be referenced by their name attribute for core profiles, or extension/name for profiles from extensions.

reporter.caption: Reporter
reporter.description: The entity from which the event or finding was first reported.

sequence.caption: Sequence Number
sequence.description: Sequence number of the event. The sequence number is a value available in some events, to make the exact ordering of events unambiguous, regardless of the event time precision.

source.caption: Source
source.description: The source of the event or finding. This can be any distinguishing name for the logical origin of the data — for example, 'CloudTrail Events', or a use case like 'Attack Simulations' or 'Vulnerability Scans'.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the event.

total_queued_duration.caption: Total Queued Duration
total_queued_duration.description: The amount of time an event spent in a queue awaiting processing. In this case, the value is the difference between processed_time and logged_time. This duration is inclusive of all queues between the originator of the event and the intended long-term storage destination of the event.

transformation_info_list.caption: Transformation Info
transformation_info_list.description: An array of transformation info that describes the mappings or transforms applied to the data.

transmit_time.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the event or finding as a subset of the source of the event. This can be any distinguishing characteristic of the data. For example 'Management Events' or 'Device Penetration Test'.

uid.caption: Event UID
uid.description: A unique identifier assigned to the OCSF event. This ID is specific to the OCSF event itself and is distinct from the original event identifier in the source system (see original_event_uid).

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OCSF schema, using Semantic Versioning Specification (SemVer). For example: 1.0.0. Event consumers use the version to determine the available event attributes.

metadata.caption: Metadata
metadata.description: The Metadata object describes the metadata associated with the event.
metadata.name: metadata

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the metric.

metric.caption: Metric
metric.description: The Metric object defines a simple name/value pair entity for a metric.
metric.name: metric

countermeasures.caption: Countermeasures
countermeasures.description: The D3FEND countermeasures that are associated with the attack technique. For example: ATT&CK Technique T1003 is addressed by Mitigation M1027, and D3FEND Technique D3-OTP.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The Mitigation name that is associated with the attack technique. For example: Password Policies, or Code Signing.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the Mitigation. For example: https://attack.mitre.org/versions/v14/mitigations/M1027.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The Mitigation ID that is associated with the attack technique. For example: M1027, or AML.M0013.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

mitigation.caption: MITRE Mitigation
mitigation.description: The MITRE Mitigation object describes the ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Mitigation ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.
mitigation.name: mitigation

references.description: ATT&CK® Mitigation to D3FEND™ Technique Mappings

base_address.caption: Base Address
base_address.description: The memory address where the module was loaded.

function_invocation.caption: Function Invocation
function_invocation.description: Details about the invocation of the function given in function_name.

function_name.caption: Function Name
function_name.description: The invoked function in the module. For load and unload events, this is the entry-point function of the module. The system calls the entry-point function whenever a process or thread loads or unloads the module.

load_type.caption: Load Type
load_type.description: The load type, normalized to the caption of the load_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

load_type_id.caption: Load Type ID
load_type_id.description: The normalized identifier for how the module was loaded in memory.

1.caption: Standard
1.description: A normal module loaded by the normal windows loading mechanism i.e. LoadLibrary.

2.caption: Non Standard
2.description: A module loaded in a way avoidant of normal windows procedures. i.e. Bootstrapped Loading/Manual Dll Loading.

3.caption: ShellCode
3.description: A raw module in process memory that is READWRITE_EXECUTE and had a thread started in its range.

4.caption: Mapped
4.description: A memory mapped file, typically created with CreatefileMapping/MapViewOfFile.

5.caption: NonStandard Backed
5.description: A module loaded in a non standard way. However, GetModuleFileName succeeds on this allocation.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The load type is not mapped. See the load_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

start_address.caption: Start Address
start_address.description: The start address of the execution.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The module type.

module.caption: Module
module.description: The Module object describes the attributes of a module.
module.name: module

boundary.caption: Boundary
boundary.description:
The boundary of the connection, normalized to the caption of 'boundary_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

For cloud connections, this translates to the traffic-boundary(same VPC, through IGW, etc.). For traditional networks, this is described as Local, Internal, or External.

boundary_id.caption: Boundary ID
boundary_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the boundary of the connection.

For cloud connections, this translates to the traffic-boundary (same VPC, through IGW, etc.). For traditional networks, this is described as Local, Internal, or External.

1.caption: Localhost
1.description: Local network traffic on the same endpoint.

10.caption: Gateway VPC
10.description: Through a gateway VPC endpoint (Nitro-based instances only)

11.caption: Internet Gateway
11.description: Through an Internet gateway (Nitro-based instances only)

2.caption: Internal
2.description: Internal network traffic between two endpoints inside network.

3.caption: External
3.description: External network traffic between two endpoints on the Internet or outside the network.

4.caption: Same VPC
4.description: Through another resource in the same VPC

5.caption: Internet/VPC Gateway
5.description: Through an Internet gateway or a gateway VPC endpoint

6.caption: Virtual Private Gateway
6.description: Through a virtual private gateway

7.caption: Intra-region VPC
7.description: Through an intra-region VPC peering connection

8.caption: Inter-region VPC
8.description: Through an inter-region VPC peering connection

9.caption: Local Gateway
9.description: Through a local gateway

99.caption: Other
99.description: The boundary is not mapped. See the boundary attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

community_uid.caption: Community ID
community_uid.description: The Community ID of the network connection.

direction.caption: Direction
direction.description: The direction of the initiated connection, traffic, or email, normalized to the caption of the direction_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

direction_id.caption: Direction ID
direction_id.description: The normalized identifier of the direction of the initiated connection, traffic, or email.

1.caption: Inbound
1.description: Inbound network connection. The connection originated from the Internet or outside network, destined for services on the inside network.

2.caption: Outbound
2.description: Outbound network connection. The connection originated from inside the network, destined for services on the Internet or outside network.

3.caption: Lateral
3.description: Lateral network connection. The connection originated from inside the network, destined for services on the inside network.

4.caption: Local
4.description: Local network connection (localhost). The connection is intra-device, originating from and destined for services running on the same device.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The direction is not mapped. See the direction attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

flag_history.caption: Connection Flag History
flag_history.description: The Connection Flag History summarizes events in a network connection. For example flags ShAD representing SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK and Data exchange.

protocol_name.caption: Protocol Name
protocol_name.description: The IP protocol name in lowercase, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: tcp or udp.

protocol_num.caption: Protocol Number
protocol_num.description: The IP protocol number, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: 6 for TCP and 17 for UDP.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The protocol version is not mapped. See the protocol_ver attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The authenticated user or service session.

tcp_flags.caption: TCP Flags
tcp_flags.description: The network connection TCP header flags (i.e., control bits).

uid.caption: Connection UID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the connection.

network_connection_info.caption: Network Connection Information
network_connection_info.description: The Network Connection Information object describes characteristics of an OSI Transport Layer communication, including TCP and UDP.
network_connection_info.name: network_connection_info

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The name of the domain that the endpoint belongs to or that corresponds to the endpoint.

fingerprints.caption: Fingerprints
fingerprints.description: Fingerprints that identify the specific application implementation on this endpoint, such as Cisco NPF or HASSH.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the endpoint.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

intermediate_ips.caption: Intermediate IP Addresses
intermediate_ips.description: The intermediate IP Addresses. For example, the IP addresses in the HTTP X-Forwarded-For header.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the endpoint, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

isp_org.caption: ISP Org
isp_org.description: The organization name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP). This represents the parent organization or company that owns/operates the ISP. For example, Comcast Corporation would be the ISP org for Xfinity internet service. This attribute helps identify the ultimate provider when ISPs operate under different brand names.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the endpoint.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.caption: MAC Vendor
mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The short name of the endpoint.

network_scope.caption: Network Scope
network_scope.description: Indicates whether the endpoint resides inside the customer’s network, outside on the Internet, or if its location relative to the customer’s network cannot be determined. The value is normalized to the caption of the network_scope_id.

network_scope_id.caption: Network Scope ID
network_scope_id.description: The normalized identifier of the endpoint’s network scope. The normalized network scope identifier indicates whether the endpoint resides inside the customer’s network, outside on the Internet, or if its location relative to the customer’s network cannot be determined.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: Unknown whether this endpoint resides within the customer’s network.

1.caption: Internal
1.description: The endpoint resides inside the customer’s network.

2.caption: External
2.description: The endpoint is on the Internet or otherwise external to the customer’s network.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The network scope is not mapped. See the network_scope attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

port.caption: Port
port.description: The port used for communication within the network connection.

proxy_endpoint.caption: Proxy Endpoint
proxy_endpoint.description: The network proxy information pertaining to a specific endpoint. This can be used to describe information pertaining to network address translation (NAT).

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

svc_name.caption: Service Name
svc_name.description: The service name in service-to-service connections. For example, AWS VPC logs the pkt-src-aws-service and pkt-dst-aws-service fields identify the connection is coming from or going to an AWS service.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The network endpoint type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the endpoint.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

network_endpoint.caption: Network Endpoint
network_endpoint.description: The Network Endpoint object describes characteristics of a network endpoint. These can be a source or destination of a network connection.
network_endpoint.name: network_endpoint

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The hostname associated with the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address associated with the network interface.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The MAC address of the network interface.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the network interface.

namespace.caption: Namespace
namespace.description: The namespace is useful in merger or acquisition situations. For example, when similar entities exist that you need to keep separate.

open_ports.caption: Open Ports
open_ports.description: The list of open ports on a network interface, including port numbers and associated protocol information.

subnet_prefix.caption: Subnet Prefix Length
subnet_prefix.description: The subnet prefix length determines the number of bits used to represent the network part of the IP address. The remaining bits are reserved for identifying individual hosts within that subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of network interface.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the network interface.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

network_interface.caption: Network Interface
network_interface.description: The Network Interface object describes the type and associated attributes of a physical or virtual network interface.
network_interface.name: network_interface

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

svc_name.description: The service name in service-to-service connections. For example, AWS VPC logs the pkt-src-aws-service and pkt-dst-aws-service fields identify the connection is coming from or going to an AWS service.

type.description: The network endpoint type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the endpoint.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

network_proxy.caption: Network Proxy Endpoint
network_proxy.description: The network proxy endpoint object describes a proxy server, which acts as an intermediary between a client requesting a resource and the server providing that resource.
network_proxy.name: network_proxy

bytes.caption: Total Bytes
bytes.description: The total number of bytes transferred in both directions (sum of bytes_in and bytes_out).

bytes_in.caption: Bytes In
bytes_in.description: The number of bytes sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

bytes_missed.caption: Bytes Missed
bytes_missed.description: The number of bytes that were missed during observation, typically due to packet loss or sampling limitations.

bytes_out.caption: Bytes Out
bytes_out.description: The number of bytes sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

chunks.caption: Chunks
chunks.description: The total number of chunks transferred in both directions (sum of chunks_in and chunks_out).

chunks_in.caption: Chunks In
chunks_in.description: The number of chunks sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

chunks_out.caption: Chunks Out
chunks_out.description: The number of chunks sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The end time of the observation or reporting period.

packets.caption: Total Packets
packets.description: The total number of packets transferred in both directions (sum of packets_in and packets_out).

packets_in.caption: Packets In
packets_in.description: The number of packets sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

packets_out.caption: Packets Out
packets_out.description: The number of packets sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The start time of the observation or reporting period.

timespan.caption: Time Span
timespan.description: The time span object representing the duration of the observation or reporting period.

network_traffic.caption: Network Traffic
network_traffic.description: The Network Traffic object describes characteristics of network traffic over a time period. The metrics represent network data transferred between source and destination during an observation window.
network_traffic.name: network_traffic

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data about the node stored as key-value pairs. Can include custom properties specific to the node.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A human-readable description of the node's purpose or meaning in the graph.

name.caption: Name
name.description: A human-readable name or label for the node. Should be descriptive and unique within the graph context.

type.caption: Type
type.description: Categorizes the node into a specific class or type. Useful for grouping and filtering nodes.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique string or numeric identifier that distinguishes this node from all others in the graph. Must be unique across all nodes.

node.caption: Node
node.description: Represents a node or a vertex in a graph structure.
node.name: node

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the note was created.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the note was last modified.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The user who created or last modified the note. Typically the same user that created the note can modify the note.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A short description of the comment, if applicable.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the note, if applicable.

note.caption: Note
note.description: Represents a note or a comment in the system. Notes can be used to provide additional context, explanations, or observations related to an event, object, or any other entity in the system. They can be created and modified by users to capture important information that may not be directly represented in the structured data.
note.name: note

object.caption: Object
object.description: An unordered collection of attributes. It defines a set of attributes available in all objects. It can be also used as a generic object to log objects that are not otherwise defined by the schema.
object.name: object

event_uid.caption: Event UID
event_uid.description: The unique identifier (metadata.uid) of the source OCSF event from which this observable was extracted. This field enables linking observables back to their originating event data when observables are stored in a separate location or system.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The full name of the observable attribute. The name is a pointer/reference to an attribute within the OCSF event data. For example: file.name. Array attributes may be represented in one of three ways. For example: resources.uid, resources[].uid, resources[0].uid.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: Contains the original and normalized reputation scores.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The observable value type name.

1.caption: Hostname
1.description:
Observable by Dictionary Type.
Unique name assigned to a device connected to a computer network. It may be a fully qualified domain name (FQDN). For example:
r2-d2.example.com.,
mx.example.com

10.caption: Resource UID
10.description:
Observable by Dictionary Type.
Resource unique identifier. For example, S3 Bucket name or EC2 Instance ID.

11.caption: Port
11.description:
Observable by Dictionary Type.
The TCP/UDP port number. For example:
80,
22.

12.caption: Subnet
12.description:
Observable by Dictionary Type.
The subnet represented in a CIDR notation, using the format network_address/prefix_length. The network_address can be in either IPv4 or IPv6 format. The prefix length indicates the number of bits used for the network portion, and the remaining bits are available for host addresses within that subnet. For example:
192.168.1.0/24,
2001:0db8:85a3:0000::/64

13.caption: Command Line
13.description:
Observable by Dictionary Attribute.
The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

14.caption: Country
14.description:
Observable by Dictionary Attribute.
The ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code.

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

15.caption: Process ID
15.description:
Observable by Dictionary Attribute.
The process identifier, as reported by the operating system. Process ID (PID) is a number used by the operating system to uniquely identify an active process.

16.caption: HTTP User-Agent
16.description:
Observable by Dictionary Attribute.
The request header that identifies the operating system and web browser.

17.caption: CWE Object: uid
17.description:
Observable by Object-Specific Attribute.
Object-specific attribute "uid" for the CWE Object.

18.caption: CVE Object: uid
18.description:
Observable by Object-Specific Attribute.
Object-specific attribute "uid" for the CVE Object.

19.caption: User Credential ID
19.description:
Observable by Dictionary Attribute.
The unique identifier of the user's credential. For example, AWS Access Key ID.

2.caption: IP Address
2.description:
Observable by Dictionary Type.
Internet Protocol address (IP address), in either IPv4 or IPv6 format. For example:
192.168.200.24,
2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334.

20.caption: Endpoint
20.description:
Observable by Object.
The Endpoint object describes a physical or virtual device that connects to and exchanges information with a computer network. Some examples of endpoints are mobile devices, desktop computers, virtual machines, embedded devices, and servers. Internet-of-Things devices—like cameras, lighting, refrigerators, security systems, smart speakers, and thermostats—are also endpoints.

21.caption: User
21.description:
Observable by Object.
The User object describes the characteristics of a user/person or a security principal.

22.caption: Email
22.description:
Observable by Object.
The Email object describes the email metadata such as sender, recipients, and direction, and can include embedded URLs and files.

23.caption: Uniform Resource Locator
23.description:
Observable by Object.
The Uniform Resource Locator (URL) object describes the characteristics of a URL.

24.caption: File
24.description:
Observable by Object.
The File object represents the metadata associated with a file stored in a computer system. It encompasses information about the file itself, including its attributes, properties, and organizational details.

25.caption: Process
25.description:
Observable by Object.
The Process object describes a running instance of a launched program.

26.caption: Geo Location
26.description:
Observable by Object.
The Geo Location object describes a geographical location, usually associated with an IP address.

27.caption: Container
27.description:
Observable by Object.
The Container object describes an instance of a specific container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

28.caption: Registry Key
28.description:
Observable by Object.
The registry key object describes a Windows registry key.

29.caption: Registry Value
29.description:
Observable by Object.
The registry value object describes a Windows registry value.

3.caption: MAC Address
3.description:
Observable by Dictionary Type.
Media Access Control (MAC) address. For example:
18:36:F3:98:4F:9A.

30.caption: Fingerprint
30.description:
Observable by Object.
The Fingerprint object provides detailed information about a fingerprint, which is a compact representation of data used to identify a longer piece of information, such as a public key, file content, or application implementation. It contains the algorithm or scheme and value of the fingerprint, enabling efficient and reliable identification of the associated data.

31.caption: User Object: uid
31.description:
Observable by Object-Specific Attribute.
Object-specific attribute "uid" for the User Object.

32.caption: Group Object: name
32.description:
Observable by Object-Specific Attribute.
Object-specific attribute "name" for the Group Object.

33.caption: Group Object: uid
33.description:
Observable by Object-Specific Attribute.
Object-specific attribute "uid" for the Group Object.

34.caption: Account Object: name
34.description:
Observable by Object-Specific Attribute.
Object-specific attribute "name" for the Account Object.

35.caption: Account Object: uid
35.description:
Observable by Object-Specific Attribute.

value.caption: Value
