observable.caption: Observable
observable.description: The observable object is a pivot element that contains related information found in many places in the event.
observable.name: observable

count.caption: Count
count.description: Integer representing the total number of times this specific value/event was observed across all occurrences. Helps establish prevalence and patterns.

timespan.caption: Time Span
timespan.description: The time window when the value or event was first observed. It is used to analyze activity patterns, detect trends, or correlate events within a specific timeframe.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The specific value, event, indicator or data point that was observed and recorded. This is the core piece of information being tracked.

observation.caption: Observation
observation.description: A record of an observed value or event that captures the timing and frequency of its occurrence. Used to track when values/events were first detected, last detected, and their total occurrence count.
observation.name: observation

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the organization, Oracle Cloud Tenancy, Google Cloud Organization, or AWS Organization. For example, Widget, Inc. or the AWS Organization name .

ou_name.caption: Org Unit Name
ou_name.description: The name of an organizational unit, Google Cloud Folder, or AWS Org Unit. For example, the GCP Project Name , or Dev_Prod_OU .

ou_uid.caption: Org Unit ID
ou_uid.description: The unique identifier of an organizational unit, Google Cloud Folder, or AWS Org Unit. For example, an Oracle Cloud Tenancy ID , AWS OU ID , or GCP Folder ID .

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the organization, Oracle Cloud Tenancy, Google Cloud Organization, or AWS Organization. For example, an AWS Org ID or Oracle Cloud Domain ID .

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

organization.caption: Organization
organization.description: The Organization object describes characteristics of an organization or company and its division if any. Additionally, it also describes cloud and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) logical hierarchies such as AWS Organizations, Google Cloud Organizations, Oracle Cloud Tenancies, and similar constructs.
organization.name: organization

country.caption: Country
country.description:
The operating system country code, as defined by the ISO 3166-1 standard (Alpha-2 code).

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The cpu architecture, the number of bits used for addressing in memory. For example: 32 or 64.

edition.caption: OS Edition
edition.description: The operating system edition. For example: Professional.

kernel_release.caption: Kernel Release
kernel_release.description: The kernel release of the operating system. On Unix-based systems, this is determined from the uname -r command output, for example "5.15.0-122-generic".

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The two letter lower case language codes, as defined by ISO 639-1. For example: en (English), de (German), or fr (French).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The operating system name.

sp_name.caption: OS Service Pack
sp_name.description: The name of the latest Service Pack.

sp_ver.caption: OS Service Pack Version
sp_ver.description: The version number of the latest Service Pack.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the operating system.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type identifier of the operating system.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OS running on the device that originated the event. For example: "Windows 10", "OS X 10.7", or "iOS 9".

os.caption: Operating System (OS)
os.description: The Operating System (OS) object describes characteristics of an OS, such as Linux or Windows.
os.name: os

architecture.caption: Architecture
architecture.description: Architecture is a shorthand name describing the type of computer hardware the packaged software is meant to run on.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

epoch.caption: Epoch
epoch.description: The software package epoch. Epoch is a way to define weighted dependencies based on version numbers.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Cryptographic hash to identify the binary instance of a software component. This can include any component such file, package, or library.

license.caption: Software License
license.description: The software license applied to this package.

license_url.caption: Software License URL
license_url.description: The URL pointing to the license applied on package or software. This is typically a LICENSE.md file within a repository.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The software package name.

package_manager.caption: Package Manager
package_manager.description: The software packager manager utilized to manage a package on a system, e.g. npm, yum, dpkg etc.

package_manager_url.caption: Package Manager URL
package_manager_url.description: The URL of the package or library at the package manager, or the specific URL or URI of an internal package manager link such as AWS CodeArtifact or Artifactory.

purl.caption: Package URL
purl.description: A purl is a URL string used to identify and locate a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

release.caption: Software Release Details
release.description: Release is the number of times a version of the software has been packaged.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The link to the specific library or package such as within GitHub, this is different from the link to the package manager where the library or package is hosted.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of software package, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

1.caption: Application
1.description: An application software package.

2.caption: Operating System
2.description: An operating system software package.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Package UID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the package or library reported by the source tool. E.g., the libId within the sbom field of an OX Security Issue or the SPDX components.*.bom-ref.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor who published the software package.

package.caption: Software Package
package.description: The Software Package object describes details about a software package.
package.name: package

encoding.caption: Encoding
encoding.description: The human-readable name of the encoding used to represent the packet data in the value field. This should match the caption associated with encoding_id. If encoding_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific encoding value.

encoding_id.caption: Encoding ID
encoding_id.description: The normalized identifier of the encoding method used to represent the packet data as a string.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The encoding format of the packet data is not known.

1.caption: Base64
1.description: The packet data is encoded using Base64.

2.caption: Hexadecimal
2.description: The packet data is encoded as a hexadecimal string representation of the raw bytes.

3.caption: URL Encoded
3.description: The packet data is encoded using percent-encoding (URL encoding).

99.caption: Other
99.description: The encoding method is not mapped. Refer to the encoding field for the original source-specific value.

end_offset.caption: End Offset
end_offset.description: The ending byte position of this packet within a capture file or stream.

format.caption: Format
format.description: The human-readable name of the packet capture file format in which the packet is stored. This should match the caption associated with format_id. If format_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific format value.

format_id.caption: Format ID
format_id.description: The normalized identifier of the packet capture format.

1.caption: PCAP
1.description: Standard libpcap/tcpdump packet capture file format.

2.caption: PCAPNG
2.description: Next-generation PCAP format that supports multiple interfaces and enhanced metadata.

3.caption: Snoop
3.description: Solaris/Unix capture format.

4.caption: ERF
4.description: Extensible Record Format used by Endace network monitoring hardware.

5.caption: NetMon
5.description: Microsoft Network Monitor capture file format.

6.caption: 5Views
6.description: Accellent 5Views packet capture format.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The packet format is not mapped. Refer to the format field for the original source-specific value.

sequence_number.caption: Sequence Number
sequence_number.description: The relative order number of this packet within its capture context (such as a PCAP file, network session, or reconstructed stream). This represents chronological capture order, distinct from both protocol-level sequencing (such as TCP sequence numbers).

source.caption: Source
source.description: The human-readable name describing how or where the packet was obtained. This should match the caption associated with source_id. If source_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific value.

source_id.caption: Source ID
source_id.description: A normalized numeric identifier that specifies how the packet was obtained or generated.

1.caption: Wire
1.description: The packet was captured directly from a network interface.

2.caption: Stream
2.description: The packet was reconstructed or derived from a stream of packets.

3.caption: Decoder
3.description: The packet was generated or extracted by a protocol decoder or analysis engine.

4.caption: TAP
4.description: The packet was captured from a physical network Test Access Point (TAP) device used for passive monitoring.

5.caption: SPAN
5.description: The packet was captured from a switch Switched Port Analyzer (SPAN) or mirror port.

6.caption: Endpoint
6.description: The packet was captured by a host-based agent or endpoint detection and response (EDR) sensor.

7.caption: Virtual
7.description: The packet was captured from a virtual network interface, virtual switch, or container network.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The packet source is not mapped. Refer to the source field for the original source-specific value.

start_offset.caption: Start Offset
start_offset.description: The starting byte position of this packet within a capture file or stream.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The actual packet data, represented as a string. The format of this string is determined by the specified encoding_id (e.g., Base64, Hexadecimal, or URL Encoded).

packet.caption: Packet
packet.description: The Packet object represents a single captured network packet and its associated metadata. It describes where the packet came from, how it is stored or encoded, and how it can be located within a capture file or stream. This object does not interpret protocol content; it only represents the captured packet data and its positioning information.
packet.name: packet

post_value.description: The parameter value after function execution.

pre_value.caption: Pre-Value

parameter.caption: Parameter

peripheral_device.description: The peripheral device object describes the properties of external, connectable, and detachable hardware.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data about the policy such as the underlying JSON policy itself or other details.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the policy.

is_applied.description: A determination if the content of a policy was applied to a target or request, or not.

name.description: The policy name. For example: AdministratorAccess Policy.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description:
The Policy object describes the policies that are applicable.

Policy attributes provide traceability to the operational state of the security product at the time that the event was captured, facilitating forensics, troubleshooting, and policy tuning/adjustments.
policy.name: policy

protocol_name.caption: Protocol Name
protocol_name.description: The IP protocol name in lowercase, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: tcp or udp.

protocol_num.caption: Protocol Number
protocol_num.description: The IP protocol number, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: 6 for TCP and 17 for UDP.

port_info.caption: Port Information
port_info.description: The Port Information object describes a port and its associated protocol details.
port_info.name: port_info

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that this process is running or hosting, if applicable. Populate when the process serves as the runtime environment for an AI agent (e.g., a Python process executing a LangChain agent or hosting an MCP server). When a process hosts multiple agents and the activity cannot be attributed to one specifically, use hosted_ai_agent_list instead.

ancestry.caption: Ancestry
ancestry.description: An array of Process Entities describing the extended parentage of this process object. Direct parent information should be expressed through the parent_process attribute. The first array element is the direct parent of this process object. Subsequent list elements go up the process parentage hierarchy. That is, the array is sorted from newest to oldest process. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

cpid.caption: Common Process Identifier
cpid.description: A unique process identifier that can be assigned deterministically by multiple system data producers.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the process was created/started.

environment_variables.caption: Environment Variables
environment_variables.description: Environment variables associated with the process.

hosted_ai_agent_list.caption: Hosted AI Agent List
hosted_ai_agent_list.description: The list of autonomous AI agents hosted by this process. Use when a single process hosts multiple agents (e.g., an IDE running several coding agents within the same host process) and the producer cannot attribute a specific activity to a single agent. When attribution is available, populate the singular ai_agent attribute instead.

hosted_services.caption: Hosted Services
hosted_services.description: The Windows services that this process is hosting.

integrity.caption: Integrity
integrity.description: The process integrity level, normalized to the caption of the integrity_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source (Windows only).

integrity_id.caption: Integrity Level
integrity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the process integrity level (Windows only).

99.caption: Other
99.description: The integrity level is not mapped. See the integrity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

lineage.caption: Lineage
lineage.description: The lineage of the process, represented by a list of paths for each ancestor process. For example: ['/usr/sbin/sshd', '/usr/bin/bash', '/usr/bin/whoami'].

loaded_modules.caption: Loaded Modules
loaded_modules.description: The list of loaded module names.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The friendly name of the process, for example: Notepad++.

parent_process.caption: Parent Process
parent_process.description: The parent process of this process object. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object, to prevent deep nesting. Additional ancestry information can be supplied in the ancestry attribute.

pid.caption: Process ID
pid.description: The process identifier, as reported by the operating system. Process ID (PID) is a number used by the operating system to uniquely identify an active process.

ptid.caption: Process Thread ID
ptid.description: The identifier of the process thread associated with the event, as returned by the operating system.

sandbox.caption: Sandbox
sandbox.description: The name of the containment jail (i.e., sandbox). For example, hardened_ps, high_security_ps, oracle_ps, netsvcs_ps, or default_ps.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The user session under which this process is running.

terminated_time.caption: Terminated Time
terminated_time.description: The time when the process was terminated.

@deprecated.message: tid is deprecated in favor of ptid. ptid has type long_t which can accommodate the thread identifiers returned by all platforms (e.g. 64-bit on MacOS).

tid.caption: Thread ID
tid.description: The identifier of the thread associated with the event, as returned by the operating system.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for this process assigned by the producer (tool).  Facilitates correlation of a process event with other events for that process.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user under which this process is running.

working_directory.caption: Working Directory
working_directory.description: The working directory of a process.

xattributes.caption: Extended Attributes
xattributes.description:
An unordered collection of zero or more name/value pairs that represent a process extended attribute.

For example: process security context attributes, process resource limits, container-specific attributes, or platform-specific process metadata not covered by standard OCSF attributes.

process.caption: Process
process.description: The Process object describes a running instance of a launched program.

cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

cpid.caption: Common Process Identifier
cpid.description: A unique process identifier that can be assigned deterministically by multiple system data producers.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the process was created/started.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The friendly name of the process, for example: Notepad++.

pid.caption: Process ID
pid.description: The process identifier, as reported by the operating system. Process ID (PID) is a number used by the operating system to uniquely identify an active process.

uid.description: A unique identifier for this process assigned by the producer (tool).  Facilitates correlation of a process event with other events for that process.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

process_entity.caption: Process Entity
process_entity.description: The Process Entity object provides critical fields for referencing a process.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

feature.caption: Feature
feature.description: The feature that reported the event.

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The two letter lower case language codes, as defined by ISO 639-1. For example: en (English), de (German), or fr (French).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the product.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The installation path of the product.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the product.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url_string.caption: URL String
url_string.description: The URL pointing towards the product.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the product.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the product, as defined by the event source. For example: 2013.1.3-beta.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The Product object describes characteristics of a software product.
product.name: product

last_used_time.caption: Last Used Time
last_used_time.description: The timestamp when this programmatic credential was last used for authentication or API access. This helps track credential usage patterns, identify dormant credentials that may pose security risks, and support credential lifecycle management. The timestamp should reflect the most recent successful authentication or API call using this credential.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type or category of programmatic credential, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source. Examples include 'API Key', 'Service Account Key', 'Access Token', 'Client Certificate', 'OAuth Token', 'Personal Access Token', etc.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the programmatic credential. This could be an API key ID, service account key ID, access token identifier, certificate serial number, or other unique identifier that distinguishes this credential from others. Examples: AWS Access Key ID, GCP Service Account Key ID, Azure Application ID, or OAuth2 token identifier.

programmatic_credential.caption: Programmatic Credential
programmatic_credential.description: The Programmatic Credential object describes service-specific credentials used for direct API access and system integration. These credentials are typically issued by individual services or platforms for accessing their APIs and resources, focusing on credential lifecycle management and usage tracking. Examples include API keys, service account keys, client certificates, and vendor-specific access tokens.
programmatic_credential.name: programmatic_credential

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of times that activity in the same logical group occurred, as reported by the related Finding.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description:
The time when the related event/finding was created.

If the related event/finding is in OCSF and is a Finding, then this value should be equal to finding_info.created_time in the corresponding Finding. If the related event/finding is in OCSF and is not a Finding, then this value should be equal to time in the corresponding event.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A description of the related event/finding.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description:
The time when the finding was first observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was first observed.
It can differ from the created_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was created.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: The Kill Chain provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description:
The time when the finding was most recently observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was most recently observed.
It can differ from the modified_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was last modified.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the related event/finding was last modified.

observables.caption: Observables
observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

product.caption: Product
product.description: Details about the product that reported the related event/finding.

product_uid.caption: Product Identifier
product_uid.description: The unique identifier of the product that reported the related event.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The related event status. Should correspond to the label of the status_id (or 'Other' status value for status_id = 99) of the related event.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated with the related event/finding.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the related event/finding.

traits.caption: Traits
traits.description: The list of key traits or characteristics extracted from the related event/finding that influenced or contributed to the overall finding's outcome.

type.caption: Type
type.description:
The type of the related event/finding.

Populate if the related event/finding is NOT in OCSF. If it is in OCSF, then utilize type_name, type_uid instead.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description:
The type of the related OCSF event, as defined by type_uid.

For example: Process Activity: Launch.

Populate if the related event/finding is in OCSF.

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description:
The unique identifier of the related OCSF event type.

For example: 100701.

Populate if the related event/finding is in OCSF.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description:
The unique identifier of the related event/finding.

If the related event/finding is in OCSF, then this value must be equal to metadata.uid in the corresponding event.

related_event.caption: Related Event/Finding
related_event.description: The Related Event object describes an event or another finding related to a finding. It may or may not be an OCSF event.
related_event.name: related_event

cis_controls.caption: CIS Controls
cis_controls.description: An array of Center for Internet Security (CIS) Controls that can be optionally mapped to provide additional remediation details.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the remediation strategy.

kb_article_list.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_article_list.description: A list of KB articles or patches related to an endpoint. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

kb_articles.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_articles.description: The KB article/s related to the entity. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of supporting URL/s, references that help describe the remediation strategy.

remediation.caption: Remediation
remediation.description: The Remediation object describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).
remediation.name: remediation

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The hostname of the entity from which the event or finding was reported.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the entity from which the event or finding was reported.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the entity from which the event or finding was reported.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: The organization properties of the entity that reported the event or finding.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the entity from which the event or finding was reported.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

reporter.caption: Reporter
reporter.description: The entity from which an event or finding was reported.
reporter.name: reporter

base_score.caption: Reputation Score
base_score.description: The reputation score as reported by the event source.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The provider of the reputation information.

score.caption: Reputation Score
score.description: The reputation score, normalized to the caption of the score_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

1.caption: Very Safe
1.description: Long history of good behavior.

2.caption: Safe
2.description: Consistently good behavior.

3.caption: Probably Safe
3.description: Reasonable history of good behavior.

4.caption: Leans Safe
4.description: Starting to establish a history of normal behavior.

5.caption: May not be Safe
5.description: No established history of normal behavior.

6.caption: Exercise Caution
6.description: Starting to establish a history of suspicious or risky behavior.

7.caption: Suspicious/Risky
7.description: A site with a history of suspicious or risky behavior. (spam, scam, potentially unwanted software, potentially malicious).

8.caption: Possibly Malicious
8.description: Strong possibility of maliciousness.

9.caption: Probably Malicious
9.description: Indicators of maliciousness.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The reputation score is not mapped. See the rep_score attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

reputation.caption: Reputation
reputation.description: The Reputation object describes the reputation/risk score of an entity (e.g. device, user, domain).
reputation.name: reputation

containers.caption: Containers
containers.description: When working with containerized applications, the set of containers which write to the standard the output of a particular logging driver. For example, this may be the set of containers involved in handling api requests and responses for a containerized application.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The additional data that is associated with the api request.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The communication flags that are associated with the api request.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique request identifier.

request.caption: Request Elements
request.description: The Request Elements object describes characteristics of an API request.
request.name: request

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the resource was created.

criticality.caption: Criticality
criticality.description:
Criticality or relative importance of this resource, normalized to the caption of criticality_id. In the case of Other, the value is defined by the event source.

Note: For versions prior to 1.9, criticality_id was not available and this is a source specific value.

criticality_id.caption: Criticality Level ID
criticality_id.description: The normalized identifier for the criticality or relative importance of this resource. Select the value that best reflects the operational and security impact if the resource were compromised or made unavailable. See the criticality sibling attribute for the corresponding human-readable label.

1.caption: Low
1.description: Minimal operational or security importance.

2.caption: Medium
2.description: Affects localized functions or specific business processes.

3.caption: High
3.description: Critical to core operations. Compromise leads to significant, but recoverable disruptions.

4.caption: Very High
4.description: Mission critical, essential to business survival. Compromise could result in catastrophic consequences.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The criticality level is not mapped. See the criticality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The device details when the resource type is a device — for example, a cloud compute instance, a laptop, or a network appliance. Provides structured device attributes (OS, type, hardware, agent) that the resource's scalar fields cannot represent — beyond what the hostname and ip attributes capture. The device.name and device.uid should match the name and uid of this objects; the device.hostname value should match the hostname attribute of this object. The top-level hostname and ip remain the primary identifiers for the device resource.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The name of the related resource group.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the resource. If the resource is a device, this should match device.hostname.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the resource, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format. If the resource is a device, this should match device.ip.

is_backed_up.caption: Back Ups Configured
is_backed_up.description: Indicates whether the device or resource has a backup enabled, such as an automated snapshot or a cloud backup. For example, this is indicated by the cloudBackupEnabled value within JAMF Pro mobile devices or the registration of an AWS ARN with the AWS Backup service.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the resource.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the resource was last modified.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the resource.

namespace.caption: Namespace
namespace.description: The namespace is useful when similar entities exist that you need to keep separate.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The details of the entity that owns the resource. Usually not the same as user that may not own the resource. For example the owner of the directory server but not a user in the directory. This object includes properties such as the owner's name, unique identifier, type, domain, and other relevant attributes that help identify the resource owner within the environment.

resource_relationship.caption: Resource Relationship
resource_relationship.description: A graph representation showing how this resource relates to and interacts with other entities in the environment. This can include parent/child relationships, dependencies, or other connections.

role.caption: Role
role.description: The role of the resource in the context of the event or finding, normalized to the caption of the role_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

role_id.caption: Role ID
role_id.description: The normalized identifier of the resource's role in the context of the event or finding.

1.caption: Target
1.description: The resource is the primary target or subject of the event/finding.

2.caption: Actor
2.description: The resource is acting as the initiator or performer in the context of the event/finding.

3.caption: Affected
3.description: The resource was impacted or affected by the event/finding.

4.caption: Related
4.description: The resource is related to or associated with the event/finding.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The role is not mapped. See the role attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the resource.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The resource type as defined by the event source.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the resource.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the resource.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user represented by this resource — for example, a cloud IAM user, a local account, or an application identity. Provides structured user attributes (email, groups, privileges) that this object's scalar fields such as name cannot represent. Distinct from owner, which identifies the entity responsible for managing the resource. The user.name value should match the name attribute of this object, user.uid should match the uid of this object.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the resource. For example 1.2.3.

resource_details.caption: Resource Details
resource_details.description: The Resource Details object describes details about a resource (including a user) affected by or related to the activity or finding. The name and/or uid should correspond to the resource for which the details pertain. Use role_id to characterize the role of the resource.
resource_details.name: resource_details

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: The numeric response sent to a request.

containers.caption: Containers
containers.description: When working with containerized applications, the set of containers which write to the standard the output of a particular logging driver. For example, this may be the set of containers involved in handling api requests and responses for a containerized application.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The additional data that is associated with the api response.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The communication flags that are associated with the api response.

message.caption: Message
message.description: The response message provided by the service or API.

response.caption: Response Elements
response.description: The Response Elements object describes characteristics of an API response.
response.name: response

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the rule that generated the event.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the rule that generated the event.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The rule type.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the rule that generated the event.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

rule.caption: Rule
rule.description: The Rule object describes characteristics of a rule associated with a policy or an event.
rule.name: rule

name.caption: Name
name.description: Name of SAN (e.g. The actual IP Address or domain.)

type.caption: Type
type.description: Type descriptor of SAN (e.g. IP Address/domain/etc.)

san.caption: Subject Alternative Name
san.description: The Subject Alternative name (SAN) object describes a SAN secured by a digital certificate
san.name: san

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the SBOM was created.

package.caption: Software Package
package.description: The software package or library that is being discovered or inventoried by an SBOM.

product.caption: Product
product.description: Details about the upstream product that generated the SBOM e.g. cdxgen or Syft.

software_components.caption: Software Components
software_components.description: The list of software components used in the software package.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of SBOM, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

1.caption: SPDX
1.description: System Package Data Exchange (SPDX®) is an open standard capable of representing systems with software components in as SBOMs (Software Bill of Materials) and other AI, data and security references supporting a range of risk management use cases. The SPDX specification is a freely available international open standard (ISO/IEC 5692:2021).

2.caption: CycloneDX
2.description: CycloneDX is an International Standard for Bill of Materials (ECMA-424).

3.caption: SWID
3.description: The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) publishes, ISO/IEC 19770-2, a standard for software identification (SWID) tags that defines a structured metadata format for describing a software product. A SWID tag document is composed of a structured set of data elements that identify the software product

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: SBOM ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the SBOM or the SBOM generation by a source tool, such as the SPDX metadata.component.bom-ref.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The specification (spec) version of the particular SBOM, e.g., 1.6.

sbom.caption: Software Bill of Materials
sbom.description: The Software Bill of Materials object describes characteristics of a generated SBOM.
sbom.name: sbom

auth_protocol.caption: Auth Protocol
auth_protocol.description: The authorization protocol as defined by the caption of auth_protocol_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

auth_protocol_id.caption: Auth Protocol ID
auth_protocol_id.description: The normalized identifier of the authorization protocol used by the SCIM resource.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The authentication protocol is not mapped. See the auth_protocol attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: When the SCIM resource was added to the service provider.

error_message.caption: Last Error Message
error_message.description: Message or code associated with the last encountered error.

is_group_provisioning_enabled.caption: SCIM Group Provisioning Enabled
is_group_provisioning_enabled.description: Indicates whether the SCIM resource is configured to provision groups, automatically or otherwise.

is_user_provisioning_enabled.caption: SCIM User Provisioning Enabled
is_user_provisioning_enabled.description: Indicates whether the SCIM resource is configured to provision users, automatically or otherwise.

last_run_time.caption: Last Sync Time
last_run_time.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful synchronization.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The most recent time when the SCIM resource was updated at the service provider.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the SCIM resource.

protocol_name.caption: Supported Protocol
protocol_name.description: The supported protocol for the SCIM resource. E.g., SAML, OIDC, or OAuth2.

rate_limit.caption: Rate Limit
rate_limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed by the SCIM resource within a specified time frame to avoid throttling.

scim_group_schema.caption: SCIM Group Schema
scim_group_schema.description: SCIM provides a schema for representing groups, identified using the following schema URI: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group as defined in RFC 7634. This attribute will capture key-value pairs for the scheme implemented in a SCIM resource.

scim_user_schema.caption: SCIM User Schema
scim_user_schema.description: SCIM provides a resource type for user resources. The core schema for user is identified using the following schema URI: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User as defined in RFC 7634. This attribute will capture key-value pairs for the scheme implemented in a SCIM resource. This object is inclusive of both the basic and Enterprise User Schema Extension.

state.caption: State
state.description: The provisioning state of the SCIM resource, normalized to the caption of the state_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

state_id.caption: State ID
state_id.description: The normalized state ID of the SCIM resource to reflect its activation status.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The provisioning state of the SCIM resource is unknown.

1.caption: Pending
1.description: The SCIM resource is Pending activation or creation.

2.caption: Active
2.description: The SCIM resource is in an Active state, or otherwise enabled.

3.caption: Failed
3.description: The SCIM resource is in a Failed state.

4.caption: Deleted
4.description: The SCIM resource is in a Deleted state, or otherwise disabled.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The provisioning state of the SCIM resource is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for a SCIM resource as defined by the service provider.

uid_alt.caption: External ID
uid_alt.description: A String that is an identifier for the resource as defined by the provisioning client. The externalId may simplify identification of a resource between the provisioning client and the service provider by allowing the client to use a filter to locate the resource with an identifier from the provisioning domain, obviating the need to store a local mapping between the provisioning domain's identifier of the resource and the identifier used by the service provider.

url_string.caption: SCIM Endpoint URL
url_string.description: The primary URL for SCIM API requests.

vendor_name.caption: Service Provider
vendor_name.description: Name of the vendor or service provider implementing SCIM. E.g., Okta, Auth0, Microsoft.

scim.caption: SCIM
scim.description: The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) Configuration object provides a structured set of attributes related to SCIM protocols used for identity provisioning and management across cloud-based platforms. It standardizes user and group provisioning details, enabling identity synchronization and lifecycle management with compatible Identity Providers (IdPs) and applications. SCIM is defined in RFC 7634.
scim.name: scim

file.caption: File
file.description: Present if this script is associated with a file. Not present in the case of a file-less script.

hashes.caption: Hashes
hashes.description: An array of the script's cryptographic hashes. Note that these hashes are calculated on the script in its original encoding, and not on the normalized UTF-8 encoding found in the script_content attribute.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Unique identifier for the script or macro, independent of the containing file, used for tracking, auditing, and security analysis.

parent_uid.caption: Parent Unique ID
parent_uid.description: This attribute relates a sub-script to a parent script having the matching uid attribute. In the case of PowerShell, sub-script execution can be identified by matching the activity correlation ID of the raw ETW events provided by the OS.

script_content.caption: Script Content
script_content.description: The script content, normalized to UTF-8 encoding irrespective of its original encoding. When emitting this attribute, it may be appropriate to truncate large scripts. When consuming this attribute, large scripts should be anticipated.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The script type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The script type is not mapped. See the type attribute which contains an event source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: Some script engines assign a unique ID to each individual execution of a given script. This attribute captures that unique ID. In the case of PowerShell, the unique ID corresponds to the ScriptBlockId in the raw ETW events provided by the OS.

script.caption: Script
script.description: The Script object describes a script or command that can be executed by a shell, script engine, or interpreter. Examples include Bash, JavsScript, PowerShell, Python, VBScript, etc. Note that the term script here denotes not only a script contained within a file but also a script or command typed interactively by a user, supplied on the command line, or provided by some other file-less mechanism.
script.name: script

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the entity.

sensor_layer.caption: Sensor Layer
sensor_layer.description: The technology or sensor layer that emitted the data, normalized to the caption of sensor_layer_id. When sensor_layer_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific label.

sensor_layer_id.caption: Sensor Layer ID
sensor_layer_id.description: The normalized identifier of the sensor layer that emitted the data. For example, use this to classify the detection surface (e.g., IPS sensor, endpoint agent, email gateway). When the type is not listed, use 99 (Other) and populate sensor_layer with the source-specific label.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The sensor layer type is Unknown.

1.caption: Network
1.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from a network, firewall, or IPS sensor.

2.caption: Endpoint
2.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from an endpoint device or agent running on an OS.

3.caption: Email
3.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from an email gateway or email security system.

4.caption: IAM
4.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from an identity and access management (IAM) system or service.

5.caption: Proxy
5.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from a proxy server (e.g., forward or reverse proxy, web gateway).

6.caption: Threat Intel
6.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from a cyber threat intelligence (CTI) system or by matching observables against a threat intelligence feed or report.

7.caption: Application
7.description: The analyzed data is emitted by, or originates from an application (e.g., web application, SaaS platform, or custom business application).

99.caption: Other
99.description: The sensor layer type is not mapped. See the sensor_layer attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the entity.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

sensor_info.caption: Sensor Information
sensor_info.description: The Sensor Information object describes a control point sensor that emits data, or originates detections. It can be part of an endpoint or agent running on an OS, a SaaS application, a network device, a Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) system, or other detection and enforcement technologies.
sensor_info.name: sensor_info

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated with the service.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the service.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the service.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the service.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The Service object describes characteristics of a service, e.g. AWS EC2.
service.name: service

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of identical sessions spawned from the same source IP, destination IP, application, and content/threat type seen over a period of time.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the session was created.

credential_uid.caption: User Credential ID
credential_uid.description: The unique identifier of the user's credential. For example, AWS Access Key ID.

expiration_reason.caption: Expiration Reason
expiration_reason.description: The reason which triggered the session expiration.

is_mfa.caption: Multi Factor Authentication
is_mfa.description: Indicates whether Multi Factor Authentication was used during authentication.

is_remote.caption: Remote
is_remote.description: The indication of whether the session is remote.

is_vpn.caption: VPN Session
is_vpn.description: The indication of whether the session is a VPN session.

issuer.caption: Issuer Details
issuer.description: The identifier of the session issuer.

terminal.caption: Terminal
terminal.description: The Pseudo Terminal associated with the session. Ex: the tty or pts value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the session.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternate unique identifier of the session. e.g. AWS ARN - arn:aws:sts::123344444444:assumed-role/Admin/example-session.

uuid.caption: UUID
uuid.description: The universally unique identifier of the session.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The Session object describes details about an authenticated session. e.g. Session Creation Time, Session Issuer.
session.name: session

author.caption: Author
author.description: The author(s) who published the software component.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Cryptographic hash to identify the binary instance of a software component.

license.caption: Software License
license.description: The software license applied to this component.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The software component name.

purl.caption: Package URL
purl.description: The Package URL (PURL) to identify the software component. This is a URL that uniquely identifies the component, including the component's name, version, and type. The URL is used to locate and retrieve the component's metadata and content.

related_component.caption: Related Component
related_component.description: The package URL (PURL) of the component that this software component has a relationship with.

relationship.caption: Relationship
relationship.description: The relationship between two software components, normalized to the caption of the relationship_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

relationship_id.caption: Relationship ID
relationship_id.description: The normalized identifier of the relationship between two software components.

1.caption: Depends On
1.description: The component is a dependency of another component. Can be used to define both direct and transitive dependencies.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The relationship is not mapped. See the relationship attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of software component, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

1.caption: Framework
1.description: A software framework.

2.caption: Library
2.description: A software library.

3.caption: Operating System
3.description: An operating system. Useful for SBOMs of container images.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

software_component.caption: Software Component
software_component.description: The Software Component object describes characteristics of a software component within a software package.
software_component.name: software_component

auth_protocol.caption: Auth Protocol
auth_protocol.description: The authorization protocol as defined by the caption of auth_protocol_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

auth_protocol_id.caption: Auth Protocol ID
auth_protocol_id.description: The normalized identifier of the authentication protocol used by the SSO resource.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The authentication protocol is not mapped. See the auth_protocol attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

certificate.caption: SAML Certificate
certificate.description: Digital Signature associated with the SSO resource, e.g., SAML X.509 certificate details.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: When the SSO resource was created.

duration_mins.caption: SSO Session Duration
duration_mins.description: The duration (in minutes) for an SSO session, after which re-authentication is required.

idle_timeout.caption: SSO Idle Timeout
idle_timeout.description: Duration (in minutes) of allowed inactivity before Single Sign-On (SSO) session expiration.

login_endpoint.caption: SSO Login Endpoint
login_endpoint.description: URL for initiating an SSO login request.

logout_endpoint.caption: SSO Logout Endpoint
logout_endpoint.description: URL for initiating an SSO logout request, allowing sessions to be terminated across applications.

metadata_endpoint.caption: SSO Metadata Endpoint
metadata_endpoint.description: URL where metadata about the SSO configuration is available (e.g., for SAML configurations).

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The most recent time when the SSO resource was updated.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the SSO resource.

protocol_name.caption: Supported Protocol
protocol_name.description: The supported protocol for the SSO resource. E.g., SAML or OIDC.

scopes.caption: Scopes

type.description: The type of the token, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. This indicates whether the token is a Client Token, API Token, or one of the protocol-specific token types.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized token type identifier. Valid values: 0 (Unknown), 1 (Ticket Granting Ticket - Kerberos), 2 (Service Ticket - Kerberos), 3 (Identity Token - OIDC), 4 (Refresh Token - OIDC), 5 (SAML Assertion), 6 (Client Token - IdP-issued), 7 (API Token - generic API keys), 99 (Other).

1.caption: Ticket Granting Ticket
1.description: Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT) for Kerberos.

2.caption: Service Ticket
2.description: Service Ticket (ST) for Kerberos.

3.caption: Identity Token
3.description: Identity (ID) Token for OIDC.

4.caption: Refresh Token
4.description: Refresh Token for OIDC.

5.caption: SAML Assertion
5.description: Authentication Assertion for SAML.

6.caption: Client Token
6.description: Client Token issued by an Identity Provider (IdP) for application authentication. Use this value for IdP-issued tokens used for service-to-service authentication. Examples: Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, Okta API tokens, Auth0 Machine-to-Machine tokens. Key characteristic: These tokens are issued by Identity Providers, not by individual services.

7.caption: API Token
7.description: A generic API token or API key used for authenticating API requests. Use this value for service-specific API authentication tokens that are NOT issued by Identity Providers. Examples: REST API keys, GraphQL API keys, Stripe API keys, Twilio API keys, AWS API keys. Key characteristic: These tokens are issued by individual services/platforms, not by Identity Providers.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique ID of a token or key, if available, such as the Secret ID of Entra ID Application Registration Client Secrets.

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or geographic region that the token or key is authorized to be used from. This may represent network-based access restrictions, geographic limitations, or other zone-based authorization policies. Examples include Okta's network zone restrictions or cloud provider region restrictions.

token.caption: Token
token.description: The Token object is the base object for representing tokens, API keys, and authentication credentials used across different contexts. This object provides common attributes for all token types, including protocol-specific authentication tokens (Kerberos, OIDC, SAML) and API/client tokens used for service authentication. When to use this object: Use the base token object directly in API activity events to represent API tokens, client tokens, or API keys used to authenticate API requests. Examples include: Okta API tokens, Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, Stripe API keys, AWS API keys. When NOT to use this object: Do NOT use the base token object for protocol-specific authentication tokens in authentication events - use authentication_token instead (which extends this object). Do NOT use token for tracking credential lifecycle and usage patterns - use programmatic_credential instead.

service_file.description:
For a user mode service (service_type_id 3 or 4) this is the executable program that the SCM launches as the service process.
For a kernel mode driver (service_type_id 1 or 2) this is the driver file loaded into the kernel at the request of the SCM.

service_start_name.caption: Service Start Name
service_start_name.description: For a user mode service, this attribute represents the name of the account under which the service is run. For a kernel mode driver, this attribute represents the object name used to load the driver.

service_start_type.caption: Service Start Type
service_start_type.description: The service start type, normalized to the caption of the service_start_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

service_start_type_id.caption: Service Start Type ID
service_start_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the service start type.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The service start type is unknown.

1.caption: Boot
1.description: A kernel mode driver loaded at boot.

2.caption: System
2.description: A kernel mode driver loaded during system startup.

3.caption: Auto
3.description: A user mode service started automatically during system startup.

4.caption: Demand
4.description: A user mode service started on demand when a process calls StartService.

5.caption: Disabled
5.description: A driver or service that cannot be started.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The service start type is not mapped. See the service_start_type attribute, which contains an event source specific value.

service_type.caption: Service Type
service_type.description: The service type, normalized to the caption of the service_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

service_type_id.caption: Service Type ID
service_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the service type.

1.caption: Kernel Driver
1.description: A kernel mode driver.

2.caption: File System Driver
2.description: A kernel mode file system minifilter.

3.caption: Own Process
3.description: A user mode service that runs in its own process.

4.caption: Share Process
4.description: A user mode service that shares a process with other services.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The service type is not mapped. See the service_type attribute, which contains an event source specific value.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the service.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the service.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

win/win_service.caption: Windows Service
win/win_service.description: The Windows Service object describes a Windows service.
win/win_service.name: win_service
